### StarCraft II (`sc2`)

Written in the batch R4 preparation, before any `sc2` unit is coded, for multiplayer at patch 5.0.17, and checked by a second researcher. Sources: the StarCraft Wiki read through its API (unit pages, Template:UnitBox, Template:UnitAgmtBox/doc), Blizzard's patch notes on news.blizzard.com, the official site starcraft2.blizzard.com, and the Liquipedia pages already in the page cache (nothing was requested from liquipedia.net).

- **Official text: the in-game description and the help panel.** The game gives each unit a short description line, and for most units its in-game help names three units it is strong against and three it is weak against. No designation line was found. No manual with unit text was found, and the official site has no unit pages: starcraft2.blizzard.com shows race overviews only, and its address for units gives a not-found page (checked 11 November 2026). Blizzard's patch notes are official text too; they seldom name a unit's job, but a design note that does counts for step 1.
- **Where to read it: Liquipedia only, and only from the cache.** Liquipedia's `Infobox unit` holds the description in its `description` field, which reads as the game's own line, and the help lists in its `strong` and `weak` fields; on the Raven and Reaper pages an editor's comment beside the strong list says the lists follow the in-game help. Cite such a page as kind wiki, with a note that the field copies in-game text. The cached unit pages, each cited under the address its cache file records:
  - https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Baneling (cached a second time as Baneling_(Legacy_of_the_Void)), https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Carrier, https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Raven_(Legacy_of_the_Void), https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Reaper_(Legacy_of_the_Void), https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Swarm_Host and https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Warp_Prism_(Legacy_of_the_Void);
  - https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Corrosive_Bile, a redirect whose file holds the Ravager page, and https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Prismatic_Alignment, a redirect whose file holds the Void Ray page.
  - The first infobox on a page is the unit; the later ones are its burrowed, cocoon or deployed forms. The Warp Prism page has a description but no strong or weak lists. The cached Auto-Turret and Changeling pages are not units of their own (plan).
- **Every other unit has no readable official line in this batch.** Step 1 gives nothing, so go on to step 2. Add an uncertain entry at roles/primary saying the in-game description could not be read (Liquipedia not requested), so the merge pass can revisit it if Mustafa allows a way to read Liquipedia.
- **Blizzard's old unit guide: unchecked.** Battle.net once had a StarCraft II game guide with a page per unit; archive.org lists a snapshot of the Adept's page from 6 March 2019 (https://web.archive.org/web/20190306085104/http://us.battle.net:80/sc2/en/game/unit/adept). It would be official text, but web.archive.org reset every connection from these sessions on 11 November 2026, so whether it holds the description or the strong and weak lists is unknown. A coder who can read a snapshot (the raw id_ form, as the R1 note says for Red Alert 2's profiles) cites it as kind official and reads it as below. It predates patch 5.0, so take role words and matchups from it, never figures. What this note says about it never stands in for reading it.
- **The StarCraft Wiki does not carry the description.** Template:UnitBox has no field for it. Its `role` field is the wiki's own words, mixing lore, the pre-release site and paraphrase: the Marine's general-purpose light infantry, the Siege Tank's three lines, from heavy infantry tank to mobile artillery, the Raven's aerial support unit, the Carrier's capital ship, the Ghost's Sniper (which would name marksman if it were official); the Adept's is empty. The ability boxes (Template:UnitAgmtBox) have a `desc` field that the template's documentation calls only a description of the ability, not game text: treat it as the wiki's words, as the R1 note does for the Command & Conquer Wiki's ability boxes. The Game Unit prose that names what a unit is strong or weak against (Zealot, Carrier, Raven pages) is the wiki's own and does not follow the help panel: the Raven's prose names the Siege Tank, while the cached help-panel list names the Dark Templar, Banshee and Roach. The quote box at the top of a unit page is a voice line or lore, often from a campaign (Abathur on the Lurker page): never role text, and never copied.
- **Roles step 1 reads the description line.** Only a role label or alias counts (vocabularies, Roles). The cached lines: the Reaper's opens with Raider (raider, if its stock speed meets raider's requires); the Swarm Host's calls it a siege unit and the Ravager's ranged artillery (siege, which must still pass its coding rule and requires); the Warp Prism's calls it a flying transport (transport, a role with no target); the Raven's aerial support names support, which the Raven can claim only if it meets support's requires (a repair tool, or a heal, repair or resupply pattern), so otherwise step 1 skips it; the Carrier's capital ship, the Void Ray's surgical strike craft and the Baneling's kamikaze unit name none.
- **Strong and weak lists (roles step 4, the secondary drop rule, matchups).** The help panel's lists name units, never kinds of target, so they give no strong-against text for step 4 and drop no role under roles.secondary, as the R1 note rules for named units in Red Alert's manual. They are official text that names a matchup: use them in counters and countered by, naming the other unit by what decides the matchup (Matchups rule 1). The Reaper's strong list is the three workers; its weak list the Stalker, Marauder and Roach.
- **So step 4 rests on the game data.** Each weapon's extra damage is tied to an attribute and added per hit before armour ([Attributes](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Attributes)). Read a bonus against Armored as a bonus against armour (anti-armour; buildings are Armored too) and a bonus against Light as a bonus against anti-infantry's target, which the word list gives as soldiers and light targets. A bonus against Biological, Mechanical, Psionic, Massive or Structure, or the Widow Mine's extra damage to shields, names none of the three targets. A weapon whose UnitBox row is marked for Air and not for Ground can hit nothing else, so it gives anti-air.
sc2.game_wide:
### StarCraft II (`sc2`)

Rewritten in the batch R4 preparation for multiplayer at patch 5.0.17, before any `sc2` unit is coded, and checked by a second researcher; it replaces the pilot list. Pages named here are on the StarCraft Wiki (https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/<Title>, read through its API) unless the bullet says otherwise; the patch notes are Blizzard's (Research notes for the r4 agents).

- **Basic orders** (no pattern): every unit has move, stop, hold position, patrol, attack and attack-move, and hold fire and weapons free (the [Hotkey](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Hotkey) page's universal abilities). Load and unload are universal keys. The game has no stance, retreat or reinforce order. Turning an ability's autocast on or off is part of that ability, not an entry of its own.
- **No veterancy:** no page read gives a versus unit ranks or experience. No `earn-veterancy`, and no ability has source veterancy.
- **Supply** (no pattern): every unit takes supply from a pool capped at 200 ([Supply](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Supply)). Leave a unit's own supply off: cost_band.raw already leaves population out. Raising the cap is not game-wide: among units only the Overlord and the Overseer do it (each UnitBox says it provides 8; Supply Depots, Pylons and town halls are buildings). Record it on those two as a passive ability, source innate, with no pattern and a fit_note naming the pattern wanted (a unit that raises its side's unit cap).
- **Attributes and bonus damage:** a unit is ground or air; light, armored or neither; biological, mechanical, both (the Hellbat) or neither (the Archon); and some also carry Massive, Psionic, Detector, Structure or Summoned, and the Mothership Heroic ([Attributes](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Attributes); the [Mothership](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Mothership) UnitBox). Bonus damage is set per attribute and added to each hit before armour; buildings count as Armored. The game has no damage_map, so armament damage takes step 5, where a bonus against Armored is a bonus against armoured targets; roles step 4 is under Official role lines.
  - **Armour class:** the attributes decide it at step 2 (Damage and armour maps, above). The Ghost has carried Light since 5.0.15: its UnitBox marks Light for versus only, while the Attributes page still lists it as neither. The Sentry is neither in versus (its UnitBox marks Light for campaign and co-op only), so it goes on to step 4. A Light, Biological creature coded bigger than small (the Mutalisk is the likely case) still comes out unarmoured by that rule: record the size break in atypical rather than pick another class.
  - **Flat armour** (armour model `damage-reduction`): the game takes each unit's armour value off every hit. The Marine's rifle hits for 6 ([Marine (StarCraft II)](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Marine_(StarCraft_II))), so stock armour of 2 or more passes the term's quarter test; mention 1 point of armour in armour.notes only.
  - **Massive:** the Archon, Carrier, Colossus, Mothership, Tempest, Battlecruiser, Thor, Brood Lord and Ultralisk ([Massive](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Massive)). Force Field, Concussive Shells and Graviton Beam do not affect them, and the ground ones break Force Fields by walking into them. Say so in their strengths, linking `immune:` to the pattern that the Sentry's or Phoenix's entry links for that ability, or naming the effect in the reason where no pattern fits. The Massive page gives them 8 transport slots, but the Archon takes 4 ([Archon (StarCraft II)](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Archon_(StarCraft_II)) UnitBox); the Colossus, Thor and Ultralisk take 8.
- **Energy** (resource `energy`): casters carry an energy bar that refills slowly and pays for their abilities, and a Terran cloak drains it while on ([Cloaking](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Cloaking)). Code energy on every unit whose UnitBox gives a maximum energy for versus (among them the Ghost, Medivac, Raven, Phoenix, Sentry, High Templar, Infestor, Viper and Overseer), and on no unit whose abilities run on cooldowns only. The Mothership is one of the latter: its UnitBox gives no energy for versus, since 5.0.12 moved its abilities to cooldowns. An energy cost is not a cooldown: give a cooldown band only from a cooldown figure. The Ghost's EMP and the High Templar's Feedback punish energy users, and the Nexus's Energy Recharge refills a unit's energy (a side-wide power, below): matchup material.
- **Cloaking and detection:** a cloaked or burrowed enemy cannot be targeted unless a detector is near, though a faint ripple can give it away and splash damage still hits it; a cloaked unit keeps its cloak while it attacks (Cloaking page). Record each cloak on its unit with `cloak`, and say in the summary that firing does not break it.
  - Always cloaked: the Dark Templar and the Observer. A passive ability, source innate; no stealth trait, because cloak is the fully invisible case (sensor traits). Since 5.0.15 the Observer can be seen while it is in Surveillance Mode (the patch notes; the box on its page agrees): say so in that mode's summary.
  - Cloak researched and switched on: the Ghost (Personal Cloaking, at the Ghost Academy) and the Banshee (Cloaking Field). Source upgrade, linking `cloak` and `upgrade-in-field`; both use energy while cloaked.
  - The Mothership's Cloaking Field is an active ability, a timed cast on a cooldown since 5.0.12, that hides friendly units and buildings near it but never the Mothership itself (Mothership page, Versus section).
  - Detectors (sensor trait `detector`): the Raven, Overseer and Observer among units; the UnitBox's detection line marks them ([Detector](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Detector)). Missile Turrets, Spore Crawlers, Photon Cannons and the Orbital Command's Scanner Sweep detect too. The Oracle's Revelation reveals for a time: an ability linking `reveal-area`. EMP shows cloaked units for a moment but not burrowed ones, and Fungal Growth shows both: say so in those abilities' summaries. In a cloaked unit's countered_by, link `sensor:detector` and name the buildings and Scanner Sweep in the reason.
- **Burrow** (pattern `burrow`, mobility trait `burrow`): the Burrow research at the Hatchery lets nearly every Zerg ground unit burrow; only the Larva, Egg, Cocoon, Broodling, Nydus Worm, Changeling and Locust cannot (cached Liquipedia page https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Burrow). The box on the StarCraft Wiki's [Burrow](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Burrow) page that leaves out the Ultralisk is old text. A burrowed unit can be targeted only with detection or under Fungal Growth, cannot move or attack unless its own entry says so, and sees less, except the Baneling and the Swarm Host. Leave burrow off units that only have the shared version. Record it on units that do more:
  - the Roach: it heals much faster while burrowed (Rapid Regeneration, which needs only the Burrow research since 4.7.1 took the extra healing away from Tunneling Claws), and it moves while burrowed only after Tunneling Claws, a separate research at the Roach Warren;
  - the Infestor (moves and casts while burrowed), the Lurker (attacks only while burrowed), the Baneling (can lie burrowed as a mine and blow up from there) and the Swarm Host (spawns Locusts while burrowed).
  - The Terran Widow Mine burrows with a button of its own: its own ability.
- **High ground** (no pattern): the game gives no combat bonus for terrain, but a ground unit cannot see up a cliff without sight from a flier or a unit standing up there, so units firing from above cannot be fired back at until they are spotted ([StarCraft II Q&A batches/40](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/StarCraft_II_Q%26A_batches/40), a Blizzard answer). Fliers see over cliffs. Leave it off. Units that cross or see past cliffs record it themselves: the Reaper's cliff jumps, the Colossus's cliff walking (the climb trait; a jump is not climb), the Stalker's Blink (`teleport`). The Colossus also sees the top of a cliff and, unlike other ranged units, can be shot from below while it stands on one ([Colossus](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Colossus)).
- **Air and ground targeting:** every unit is ground or air (Attributes page), and each weapon row of the UnitBox is marked for Ground, Air or both. The game has one air layer, which only weapons marked for Air reach.
  - can_target: a Ground mark is the weapon's own target line, since the row names the weapon, so it lists infantry and ground vehicles, and structures too when the weapon's family allows them (can_target step 3); an Air mark lists low air and high air. The game has no ships: never naval.
  - Mobility: every flier can stop and hold still (stop and hold position are universal orders), so code hovering flight, not jet, and add a fit_note at mobility/base saying that the game's fliers hover yet only weapons marked for Air reach them. Slow fliers (the Overlord, Overseer, Observer, Brood Lord, Carrier and Mothership among them) break that term's speed rule: record the break in atypical.
  - Matchups: name fliers as `class:aircraft` (one layer; Matchups rule 2).
  - The Colossus is a ground unit that weapons marked for Air can also hit; the Colossus page says Blizzard confirmed it. Say so in its weaknesses and put anti-air units in its countered_by. A unit whose mode changes its layer (the Viking lands in assault mode) gives the layer per mode.
- **Add-ons** (no pattern): a Barracks, Factory or Starport takes a Tech Lab (advanced units and research) or a Reactor (two units at once), never both ([Tech lab](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Tech_lab), [Reactor](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Reactor)). Not a tier step (tier map). Name a needed Tech Lab in tier.basis; record nothing on the unit.
- **Warp-in** (`drop-in-from-above` would fit; left off): once Warp Gate is researched, the Zealot, Sentry, Stalker, Adept, Dark Templar and High Templar can be warped onto any power field of a Pylon or of a Warp Prism in phasing mode ([Gateway](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Gateway), Warp Gate section). Since 5.0.17 a warp takes 3.6 seconds in fast fields and 11 in slow ones; the page's times are older. Leave warp-in off those units. The phasing mode that makes the field is the Warp Prism's own mode.
- **Larva and eggs** (no pattern): most Zerg units hatch from Larva at a Hatchery, Lair or Hive; the Queen is not made from Larva, and the Baneling, Ravager, Lurker, Overseer and Brood Lord are morphed from other units ([Larva (StarCraft II)](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Larva_(StarCraft_II))). Production stays off every unit; the Larva and the Cocoon are not units (plan). One Zergling purchase gives two for 50 minerals ([Zergling (StarCraft II)](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Zergling_(StarCraft_II)) UnitBox): code body.count 2 and cost_band.raw 50, the price of one purchase; each Zergling moves on its own, so the crew model stays solo.
- **Morphing and merging: not game-wide.** Five units turn, at a price, into another unit that the plan codes on its own: Zergling to Baneling, Roach to Ravager, Hydralisk to Lurker, Corruptor to Brood Lord, Overlord to Overseer. The button belongs to the parent: record it there as an active ability, source innate (name the tech it needs in the summary), linking `upgrade-in-field`, whose morph-up variant is this case (pay, wait helpless, stay the new unit for good). Two templar merge into an Archon for no resources: record the merge on both templar units, the Dark Templar and the High Templar, as an active ability, source innate, linking `upgrade-in-field` too (the merge takes some seconds, per the Archon UnitBox, and has no way back), with a fit_note at its patterns naming what that pattern leaves out (two units merge into one stronger unit). The child names its parent in tier.basis and cost_band.basis, and its price includes the parent's (cost_thresholds basis). The Overlord's transport morph only adds seats to the same unit (Transports, below). The Hellion and the Hellbat switch back and forth at will, which is no morph: the tier notes above treat the Hellbat as the Hellion's second mode.
- **Creep** (no pattern): Zerg ground units move faster on creep, most by 30 percent (the UnitBox's creep multiplier: 1.3 for the Zergling); Queens and some others gain far more, Drones and fliers nothing, and creep belongs to no player, so an enemy Zerg uses it too ([Creep](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Creep)). Speeds are taken off creep; say in mobility.notes when a unit's multiplier differs from the usual. Spreading creep belongs to the units that do it (the Overlord's Generate Creep, and the unit that places creep tumours).
- **Transports** (universal keys; `carry-passengers` on the carrier): the Medivac and the Warp Prism have 8 cargo slots, and an Overlord gets 8 once it buys its own transport morph (Mutate Ventral Sacs, which needs a Lair; since Legacy of the Void each Overlord buys it for itself: [Overlord (StarCraft II)](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Overlord_(StarCraft_II))).
  - A rider fills slots by its size, from 1 (the Marine, the Zergling) to 8 (the Colossus, the Thor, the Ultralisk); the Archon, though Massive, takes 4. Each UnitBox gives the unit's size.
  - Code crew.passengers.seats as the carrier's slot count, kind passenger-cargo, since no page shows riders firing out; give the slot sizes in crew.notes. The Overlord's seats come only from that purchase, so its seat passive is source upgrade and links `carry-passengers` and `upgrade-in-field`.
  - Loading and unloading are universal keys. The Load Nearby command that 5.0.16 gave the Medivac, Warp Prism and Overlord was taken out again by the 5.0.16b hotfix.
  - Buildings that hold units are not coded, and the extra point of range a soldier gets in a Bunker stays off (range bands use the unit in the open). No page read says what happens to riders when a Medivac, Warp Prism or Overlord is destroyed: write nothing about it unless the unit's own page does.
- **Plasma shields** (armour model `regen-shield`): every Protoss unit has shields over its health; they refill quickly after a short spell without damage, suffer whatever bonus damage the unit beneath would take, and EMP drains them ([Plasma shield](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Plasma_shield)). Code regen-shield on each Protoss unit, as the term's examples say, and put Forge shield levels in armour.notes.
- **Zerg regeneration** (armour model `self-repair`): Zerg units slowly regain health at one shared rate (the UnitBox's hit point regen line), except the Mutalisk, whose versus line is several times higher ([Mutalisk (StarCraft II)](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Mutalisk_(StarCraft_II))). Code self-repair on each Zerg unit; say in armour.notes that it is slow and shared by the race, and give the Mutalisk's faster rate in its own armour.notes. The Roach heals much faster while burrowed (Burrow, above). Terran and Protoss health does not come back on its own, except the Reaper's, which heals out of combat by its in-game description (cached Liquipedia Reaper page): code self-repair on the Reaper.
- **Repair and healing by others** (nothing on the unit that receives it): SCVs and MULEs repair any friendly mechanical unit, Protoss ones included, and Terran buildings ([SCV (StarCraft II)](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/SCV_(StarCraft_II))); Medivacs heal friendly biological units. Record healing only on the unit that does it (the Medivac: `repair-allies`); workers and buildings are not coded, and being repairable is no armour model.
- **Class-wide upgrades** (side-wide, left off): weapon and armour levels bought for a whole class of units at the Engineering Bay (Terran infantry), Armory (vehicles and ships), Evolution Chamber (Zerg ground), Spire (Zerg fliers), Forge (Protoss ground units and every shield) and Cybernetics Core (Protoss air) (their pages). Bands use the stock unit; name levels in notes only where they turn a matchup.
- **Research for one unit type:** research done once at a building (Stimpack, Concussive Shells, Personal Cloaking, Blink, Charge, Burrow and the like) is source upgrade, even though it reaches every unit of the type (ability sources tie-break). It reaches units already fielded (5.0.15 fixed a bug that left units already reached by the Hi-Sec Auto Tracking research showing the old level on their icons), so a button or weapon it adds links `upgrade-in-field` (Paired entries). Research that only changes numbers (speed, range, health) goes in that field's notes.
- **Side-wide powers** (left off every unit): the Orbital Command's Scanner Sweep (reveals an area, hidden units included), MULE and Extra Supplies; the Nexus's Chrono Boost, Strategic Recall (pulls units back to a Nexus) and Energy Recharge ([Orbital command](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Orbital_command), [Nexus](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Nexus)). None gives named unit types a new button, so no ability has source commander-power. Name them in matchups where they matter: Scanner Sweep against cloaked units, Energy Recharge for casters, Recall for a Protoss army that must escape.
- **Map features** (no pattern): a ground unit next to a Xel'Naga tower gives its side the tower's wide view; burrowed units and fliers cannot hold a tower, cloaked units can ([Xel'naga tower](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Xel%27naga_tower)). Leave it off.
- **Caps** (availability): only the Mothership has a cap of its own, one per player at a time (Mothership page): availability limited, not unique, since it is no hero. Its Heroic attribute only shuts out some spells, such as Neural Parasite ([Infestor](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Infestor), Neural Parasite box). Every other unit is open; the supply cap is shared.
sc2.research_notes:
### StarCraft II (`sc2`)

Rewritten in the batch R4 preparation (11 November 2026) for multiplayer at patch 5.0.17. It replaces step 1's StarCraft II bullet here, its Liquipedia bullet under Choices that need a look and its two SC2 Speed bullets.

- **Liquipedia: the cached pages only.** Request nothing from liquipedia.net, neither its pages nor its API: its terms do not allow automated reading of its pages, and Mustafa decides how it may be read (step 1's advice to follow its API terms no longer applies). The pages already in the page cache (.cache/sources/liquipedia.net/) may be read, named and cited, each under the address its cache file records: the unit pages listed under Official role lines; Burrow, Resources, Terran Tech Tree (Legacy of the Void) and Stimpack; the Reaper's SCAbility/Jet_Pack and SCAbility/KD8_Charge; and the spell pages Cloak, Force Field, Psionic Storm, Revelation, Scanner Sweep, Tactical Nuke and Time Warp. Of a Liquipedia infobox, only the `description` field and the help lists are official text (Official role lines).
- **The StarCraft Wiki** (starcraft.fandom.com, read through https://starcraft.fandom.com/api.php, since a plain page request gets HTTP 403). Its infoboxes (Template:UnitBox) have costmin, costgas, supply, produced, req and speed, and the attributes under type.
  - A line can hold several values, each marked with where it holds: Versus, a campaign, Co-op, Nova Covert Ops, or an older expansion (WoL, HotS). Take the value marked Versus, or else the one with no mark; never a Co-op or campaign value. On the [Ghost (StarCraft II)](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Ghost_(StarCraft_II)) UnitBox, the unmarked speed 3.85 stands beside 2.25 marked for WoL and HotS, and the unmarked gas 125 beside 150 marked for the WoL campaign.
  - Versus speeds, weapon cooldowns and the times in the ability boxes are on the Faster scale (the Stalker's Blink box on the [Blink](https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Blink) page gives the Legacy of the Void cooldown of 7). The per-second regeneration lines (hit points, energy, the Roach's burrowed rate) are on the Normal scale: the Roach's 5 is Blizzard's 7 a second divided by 1.4. The registry's speed_reference gives the conversions.
  - Unit pages are long, mostly campaign, co-op, lore and navigation boxes (the Siege tank page's rendered HTML runs to about 360,000 characters). Read the UnitBox in the source (the page reader's --source) and the Versus section's boxes in the rendered page by searching, not whole.
- **Speed** (replaces step 1's two SC2 Speed bullets). Use base speed, with no creep, Stimpack or speed upgrades: Stimpack is an ability, creep is game-wide and recorded on no unit, and research that only adds speed goes in mobility.notes. Keep one game speed throughout, Faster, as the versus speed lines give it.
- **Patch notes: Blizzard's, newest first.** Research patch 5.0.17, still the newest on 11 November 2026, and take each value from the newest note that changes it: 5.0.17 of 7 October 2026 (https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24309308/starcraft-ii-5-0-17-patch-notes); the 5.0.16b hotfix of 16 July 2026 (https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24291949/starcraft-ii-5-0-16b-hotfix-patch-notes); the 5.0.16 hotfix of 30 June 2026 (https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24289266/starcraft-ii-5-0-16-hotfix-patch-notes); 5.0.16 of 22 June 2026 (https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24259080/starcraft-ii-5-0-16-patch-notes); the 5.0.15 hotfix of 8 October 2025 (https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24240447/starcraft-ii-5-0-15-hotfix-patch-notes); 5.0.15 of 30 September 2025 (https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24225313/starcraft-ii-5-0-15-patch-notes). Older notes are on the same feed, https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/feed/starcraft-2 (plain HTML), such as 4.7.1 for the Roach.
  - 5.0.17 takes most of 5.0.16's balance changes back to 5.0.15, item by item. What its list leaves out still stands, such as the 5.0.16 lines on Changelings (each starts with a copy of its Overseer's queued orders, and one dying kills the Changelings near it) and on Neural Parasite cast on an SCV that is building (it lasts until the building is done).
  - The 5.0.16b hotfix had already removed Load Nearby and set the Ghost back to 2 supply. The 5.0.15 hotfix set Psionic Storm, the Brood Lord's speed and the Ghost's health.
  - Cite Blizzard's article for every patched value. The wiki's own copy of the notes (StarCraft II version history/Patch 5.0.0) leaves out the Ghost's 5.0.17 speed and gives Psionic Storm 112, where Blizzard's article says 110.

### Halo Wars (`hw1`)

Written in batch R4 preparation, before any `hw1` unit is coded, from the 2009 manual and quick reference chart (Microsoft PDFs that Halopedia hosts), Halopedia's Halo Wars building tables and its copies of the official site's unit pages, and the Definitive Edition's game data.

- **Designation: the in-game role line.** The game gives every unit a short role text. Halopedia's Halo Wars building tables give it in their Type column, and the unit's rollover text in their Description column. Both columns are game text: their rows repeat the quotes Halopedia marks as in-game descriptions (the Covenant Warehouse and Covenant Temple pages), and each unit's `RoleTextID` in the game data (`squads.xml`) decodes to its Type word. The decoding goes through Halo Wars 2's legacy string table, which keeps the first game's role ids but has replaced some other Halo Wars strings, so it backs the tables and never stands in for them. Cite a table as kind wiki, with a note that its Type and Description columns copy the in-game text.
  - Pages: https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Barracks, https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Vehicle_Depot, https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Airpad, https://www.halopedia.org/Firebase (the Warthog and the leader units Elephant, Cyclops and Gremlin), https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Hall, https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Factory, https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Summit, https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Citadel (Scarab, Suicide Grunts, Brutes, Elite Honor Guard) and https://www.halopedia.org/Covenant_Temple (the three Covenant leaders).
  - Read only the table under the Halo Wars heading. The UNSC Barracks, Airpad and Firebase pages also hold Halo Wars 2 tables that give units of the same name other types (Core Infantry for Marines, Core Aircraft for the Hornet, Heavy Air for the Vulture, Anti-Vehicle Mech for the Cyclops).
  - The lines: Main Infantry (Marines, ODSTs, Grunt squad), Main Vehicle (Scorpion, Grizzly, Wraith), Main Air (Hornet, Hawk, Banshee), Anti-Infantry (Flamethrower, Jackal), Anti-Vehicle (Cobra, Hunter), Anti-Air (Wolverine, Vampire), Scout (Warthog, Ghost, Brute Chopper), Building Killer (Cyclops, Locust), Combat Support (Gremlin), Support Unit (Engineer), Mobile Mini-Base (Elephant), Special Forces (Spartan, Brutes, Elite Honor Guard, Suicide Grunts), Uber Unit (Vulture, Scarab), Leader (Arbiter, Brute Chieftain, Prophet of Regret). Every unit has one, so step 1 never falls back to a one-line description.
  - This line alone is the designation. The official site's Role lines and the manual's entries are other official text (below): they never replace it at step 1.
- **Roles step 1: which lines name a role.**
  - Anti-Infantry: anti-infantry. Anti-Vehicle: anti-armour (an alias). Anti-Air: anti-air. Scout: scout. Support Unit: support (the Engineer repairs and heals).
  - These name none, so step 1 goes on: Main Infantry, Main Vehicle, Main Air, Building Killer (no label or alias; not siege), Combat Support (the roles word list says combat support names no role), Mobile Mini-Base, Special Forces, Uber Unit and Leader.
  - Troop Transport (a transport alias) belongs only to the Pelican and Spirit dropships, which no building trains: they are not researched.
- **Other official text.** It never replaces the role line at step 1, but it counts at roles.secondary step 1 (a label or alias anywhere in it, in any word form), as strong-against text at roles.primary step 4 and roles.secondary step 3, and for the rule that drops a role whose target the text calls a weak point.
  - **The manual** (Microsoft, 2009): Halopedia's copy https://halo.wiki.gallery/images/4/4d/HW_Manual.pdf, linked from https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars_manual, which names the download.microsoft.com original. Unit entries: UNSC units on PDF pages 14 to 17, Covenant leaders on 17 to 19, Covenant units on 21 to 23. Each gives the building, the tech level, a sentence or two, the starting special attack and the upgrades. Kind official. Some Halopedia unit pages quote an entry in a quote box credited to the manual (https://www.halopedia.org/Hornet): cite such a page as kind wiki, with a note naming the manual and its page.
  - **The quick reference chart** (Xbox.com, 2009): https://halo.wiki.gallery/images/9/91/HW_TechTree.pdf, from https://www.halopedia.org/File:HW_TechTree.pdf. Four sheets give every unit, building and upgrade its tech level and a short phrase. Kind official.
  - **Reading the two PDFs.** Entries stand side by side in columns, and pdftotext mixes them in either mode: plain mode puts the Cobra's text under the Elephant's heading on PDF page 16, and on PDF page 23 the note that Spartans cannot jack a unit belongs to the Scarab, not to the Vampire printed beside it (word positions from `pdftotext -bbox` show the column). Match each entry's name, building and tech level before using its text.
  - **The official site's unit pages.** halowars.com is gone; Halopedia copies its pages word for word at https://www.halopedia.org/Archive:Halowars.com/UNSC and https://www.halopedia.org/Archive:Halowars.com/Covenant. Cite those as kind wiki, with a note naming the original site. Nine units have a Role line: Marines (all purpose), Flamethrower (anti-infantry), Spartan (special forces), Scorpion (main battle tank), Wolverine (anti-air), Cobra (anti-armor), Hornet (antipersonnel), Ghost (scouting) and Engineer (healing). The copies were captured in 2010 and 2011 and miss the Covenant leaders and every leader's own unit.
  - **The rollover texts** in the tables' Description column.
  - **Not official:** Halopedia's own prose, its Tactics and Strategy sections, the leaders' Gameplay pages and the unit infobox's role field (the Type-25 Wraith infobox's artillery tank is the wiki's words, as is the personnel carrier of the M312 Elephant page).
- **Role words in that text** (roles.secondary step 1; each role's requires and coding rule still bind):
  - scout: the Warthog (site: valued for reconnaissance; rollover: a fast scout), the Ghost (site: a scout vehicle, Role scouting; rollover: a recon unit), the Brute Chopper (rollover: a recon unit), the Banshee (site: it scouts) and Jackals (site: scouting roles);
  - raider, through harasser in word form: the Ghost (site: harassing infantry) and the Banshee (site: it harasses);
  - marksman, through sniper in word form: Jackals (site: sniping roles), though marksman's coding rule needs a sniper-family weapon that reaches long;
  - anti-air: the Hornet (site: a versatile anti-air unit), the Wolverine and the Vampire (site);
  - anti-infantry: the Hornet (Role antipersonnel);
  - anti-armour: Hunters (site: an anti-vehicle role) and the Cobra (rollover: an anti-vehicle threat);
  - siege, through artillery: the Cobra's deployed form (manual and rollover: an artillery unit, good against buildings); siege's coding rule decides.
  - These name none: the Scorpion's site heading (M808B Main Battle Artillery Tank), since siege's coding rule rejects a gun aimed straight at targets in view; the Wraith's site text, which says that, for all its artillery-style gun, it behaves like a tank; the Vulture's flying assault tank and the Scarab's assault vehicles (assault alone names no role). The Wraith's anti-personnel plasma cannons are a label on a second weapon: it counts for that weapon at roles.secondary step 3, not as a label of the unit.
- **Strong-against and weak-against.** No Strong vs or Weak vs lines exist. Read these, in this order of weight:
  1. **The manual's triangle** (PDF page 7, Unit Types): of three kinds of mainline unit, each is especially good against one other: vehicles beat infantry, infantry beats aircraft, aircraft beat vehicles; specialised units are left to their own entries. It is official strong-against text only for units whose role line is Main Infantry, Main Vehicle or Main Air (the manual, the chart and the rollovers call them mainline or main): Marines, ODSTs and Grunts against air; the Scorpion, Grizzly and Wraith against infantry; the Hornet, Hawk and Banshee against vehicles, which means armour.
  2. **Each unit's own wording.** Counter-infantry, counter-vehicle, counter-air and counter-building (manual, chart, rollovers) are strong-against wording for infantry, armour, air and structures (structures give no anti role), not role labels. Other strong wording: the Flamethrower (all infantry), the Jackal and the Ghost (infantry), the Hunter (even tanks), the Gremlin (ground vehicles), the Brute Chieftain (heavy vehicles), the Wolverine and the Vampire (air), the Vulture (ground troops, site) and the Wraith (armour columns and infantry, armour named first). Weak wording: the Gremlin is less effective against infantry (rollover); the Scorpion's main gun struggles against some heavily armoured vehicles (site), which drops anti-armour; the slow Vulture is easy prey for anti-air guns and enemy fliers (site), which drops anti-air. The Wolverine's weakness to anti-armour attacks names a kind of attack, not of target: no role to drop.
  3. **Words that name no single kind give nothing:** the Marines (most everything), the Hornet (most any enemy), the Banshee (ground and air forces alike), the Vulture's manual entry, the Scarab (all classes of target) and the Elite Honor Guard (any target).
  - Target words: infantry, troops, soldiers and organic targets mean infantry; vehicles, tanks and armour mean armour; air, aircraft and air units mean air; buildings, bases and structures match no anti role.
- **Bonus from the game data (roles step 4).** The damage table (`weapontypes.xml`) gives every weapon type a multiplier against each target category, and each weapon's type is in its unit's tactics file (addresses under the research notes). A multiplier above 1 is extra damage, by step 4's clause on resist tables. Read the categories as kinds: Light, LightArmored and CovenantLeader are infantry, Medium and Heavy are armour, MediumAir is air; Building, Shielded (worn by infantry, vehicles and a leader alike), Flood and the in-cover categories name no kind. Where the categories of one kind differ, use the largest.
  - Examples: SmallArms (the Marines' rifle) is above 1 against the three infantry categories, Medium and Shielded, most of all against Light. AntiAir is far above 1 against MediumAir and a little above against infantry. ArmorPiercing is far above against Medium and Heavy and well above against MediumAir. Explosive (the Scorpion's and Wraith's main guns) is a little above against infantry, armour and buildings, most against Medium and Heavy, and exactly 1 against MediumAir, Shielded and Flood.
  - The table and official text both count; then step 4's tie rule and each role's requires decide. The Scorpion's gun has its largest bonus against armour, but explosive damage fails anti-armour's requires, so step 4 skips it and anti-infantry remains, as the triangle says.
- **Sides and leaders.** Text about one leader's version of a unit counts only for that version. Where a unit is recorded once for its side although a leader changes it (the Brute Chieftain's Grunt squads are led by a Brute, the other leaders' by an Elite), read only the text that every version shares.
hw1.game_wide:
### Halo Wars (`hw1`)

Written in batch R4 preparation, before any `hw1` unit is coded, from the 2009 manual (PDF pages 6 to 23), the quick reference chart, the Halopedia pages named below (https://www.halopedia.org/<Title>, read through the API), Halo Nation's Standard (Halo Wars), Deathmatch (Halo Wars) and Supplies pages, and the Definitive Edition's game data (addresses under the research notes).

- **Basic orders** (no pattern): select, move, attack, cancel, rally points, control groups and camera moves. The attack button also gathers, and units open fire by themselves on nearby enemies or on attackers (manual, PDF page 6; HW:Control schemes, both control lists). Neither list nor the manual has stances, attack-move, patrol, a retreat or a reinforce order. Leave them off.
  - The special attack (Y on the controller, R on PC) is not a basic order: each unit has its own, on a recharge timer, and the button fires the specials of every selected unit (manual, PDF page 6). Record it on the unit.
- **Veterancy** (`earn-veterancy`): every unit earns up to three stars by fighting, each raising its attack, rate of fire, defence and health (Halo Wars page, Game concepts, Veterancy points). In the game data every unit has three ranks with experience thresholds, plus two more levels with no threshold, each raising the damage it deals and cutting the damage it takes (`objects.xml`, the Veterancy lines). Leave it off every unit.
  - The same section says upgrading a unit also gives stars, and in the data each unit upgrade raises a level stored on the squad. Treat that as the upgrade, not as rank (see Unit upgrades).
  - A vehicle a Spartan has boarded can climb past three (same section). That belongs to the Spartan's boarding (see Spartans and vehicles), not to the vehicle.
  - The Engineer's thresholds are all zero in the data and it has no weapon, so whether it ranks at all is unclear: an uncertain entry if it matters.
- **Unit upgrades** (`upgrade-in-field` where they add a weapon or a button): every unit has up to three upgrades, each bought once at the building that makes it (Halo Nation's Standard page; the manual's unit entries). They reach every unit of the type, those already in the field included (the rollovers say all Gremlins, all Elephants; in the data each upgrade is a tech aimed at the unit type). So an added weapon is an acquired weapon, and an added button (the Flamethrower's Flash Bang, the Wraith's Scorch, the Banshee's Boost, the Brutes' Jump Pack) is an ability with source upgrade, both linking `upgrade-in-field` (Paired entries). Upgrades that only change numbers go in notes. Upgrade levels are not tiers (the tiers word list names Halo Wars for this).
  - The Marines' third upgrade, the Medic, heals only its own squad once a fight is over (manual, PDF page 14; UNSC Barracks table): it belongs to the Marines' upgrades, never to `repair-allies`.
  - The super upgrades turn a unit type into a stronger one for one leader: Marines into ODSTs (Cutter), Scorpions into Grizzlies (Forge), Hornets into Hawks (Anders) (manual; the leaders' Gameplay pages). A coded super unit costs what its base unit costs (cost_band.raw leaves out upgrades bought for every unit of the type), and its gate is the tech level its upgrade needs: 3 for ODSTs, 4 for Grizzlies and Hawks (`techs.xml`; chart, sheet 1).
  - Side-wide research stays off: the Field Armory's Adrenaline (faster infantry), Reserves (faster training) and Reinforcements (more population), the Temple's Forerunner Shield (faster shield recharge for every Covenant unit) and Followers, and the turret upgrades.
- **Leaders** (subfactions in the registry): each player picks one of the side's three leaders (manual, PDF pages 9, 11, 12 and 17 to 19).
  - A UNSC leader never takes the field in skirmish: each brings a leader power, a special unit, a super upgrade and an economy bonus. The economy bonuses stay off.
  - A Covenant leader is a hero on the field: placed for free when the first Temple is finished, one at a time, outside the population count, and bought again at the Temple after a death (Covenant Temple page; manual). Its powers (the Arbiter's Rage, the Chieftain's Vortex, the Prophet's Cleansing beam) cost supplies for every second they run (manual): record them on the leader unit, source innate, with the running cost in the summary.
- **UNSC leader powers** (side-wide; leave them off): picked from the radial menu of the orbiting ship (Leader power page). MAC Blast and ODST Drop (Cutter; the drop brings new ODST squads to the spot the player picks, once the Marines have their last upgrade: a call-in, like Red Alert's paratroopers, not a button of the ODSTs), Carpet Bomb (Forge), Cryo Bomb (Anders; it freezes units in place and makes frozen aircraft crash, Ellen Anders/Gameplay page), and for every UNSC leader Disruption Bomb (blocks leader powers inside a small area for some time), Heal and Repair (restores units and mends buildings in a chosen area, though not those in combat; its own page) and Pelican Transport (dropships lift a small group of units elsewhere). None gives a named unit type a new button, so no `hw1` ability has source commander-power.
- **Covenant Gravity Lift** (no pattern): every Covenant base has one; units sent into it come out beside the leader, the Scarab excepted, and it can recall the leader for a fee (manual, PDF page 20; Covenant Citadel page). A base feature: leave it off.
- **Supply crates** (picking one up is the universal pick-up key): crates lie on the map at the start and are left by destroyed neutral bases; only infantry and scout units can collect them (manual, PDF page 8; Resources page; the Warthog's, Ghost's and Brute Chopper's manual entries). Leave collecting off, and never code `gather-resources` for it: nobody carries anything back.
- **Garrisoning map structures** (`carry-passengers` on the structure, never on the riders): infantry can enter some neutral map structures and wrecks and fight from inside. Sniper Towers make their occupants harder to kill and longer-reaching, and other structures give the holder a tech level, supplies, population room or a map feature (Covenant watchtower page; Halo Nation's Standard page; the Forerunner secondary reactor, supply elevator and lifesupport pod pages). Leave it off.
  - In the data the tactics files of most infantry hold in-cover copies of their weapons that reach much further (the Marines' rifle: 60 against 25), and the damage table has in-cover categories: that is this garrison and cover effect. Never code the in-cover weapons; range bands use the weapon in the open, and the bonus goes in notes where it matters.
- **Transports** (no pattern for the game): no unit buildable in skirmish carries others; in the data only the Pelican and Spirit dropships have seats (`objects.xml`, the Contain lines). Armies move by Pelican Transport (a UNSC power) and the Gravity Lift (a Covenant base feature). Give no `hw1` unit passenger seats for them.
  - The Elephant trains infantry once deployed but carries none (manual, PDF page 16; the data gives it training commands and no seats). Halopedia's M312 Elephant page calls it a personnel carrier in its own words: give it no seats for that.
- **Spartans and vehicles** (not game-wide): the Spartan's Jack special takes an enemy vehicle (`hijack-vehicle`), and the same special on a friendly vehicle boards it to boost it (`join-ally-crew`). Only one Spartan fits in a vehicle, and Scarabs and Vultures cannot be taken (manual, PDF page 15 for the Spartan and PDF page 23 for the Scarab; Boarding page). The data agrees: every other buildable vehicle and aircraft, the Vampire included, carries a Spartan boarding type (`objects.xml`). Record both on the Spartan. The vehicles get no passenger seats for it; the Scarab and the Vulture say in strengths that they cannot be taken.
- **Shields** (armour model `regen-shield` where the stock unit has one): Covenant shields recharge, and the Temple's Forerunner Shield speeds that up (Covenant Temple page; manual, PDF page 20). In the data only three units read have a shield as bought: the Spartan, the Locust and the Prophet of Regret. The Wraith's Heavy Shield, the Ghost's Scout Shield, the Elite Honor Guard's Personal Shield, the Jackal's Defense Gauntlet and the Hunter's Bonded Shield come with upgrades: put those in armour.notes (Stock values). The manual gives the Spartan an energy shield, but no page read shows it recharging (Halopedia's line saying so sits in a hidden comment of the Halo Wars page): check the Spartan's own pages before coding `regen-shield`.
- **Repair and healing** (no pattern for the game): healing comes from Heal and Repair (a UNSC power), from units that heal others (the Engineer; the Cyclops after its Repair Kit upgrade) and from Covenant shields recharging. No page read says units heal on their own: code self-repair only from a unit's own page. A unit that heals others records it on itself (`repair-allies`); the Engineer cannot mend itself (the official site's Engineer entry).
- **Population and caps** (no pattern): every unit takes population room (manual, PDF page 7). Spartans are capped at three and take none, and a Covenant leader is one at a time and takes none (manual; the notes of the UNSC Barracks and Covenant Temple tables): record those caps in availability and tier.basis. The data keeps them in pools of their own (`leaders.xml`: Spartan, Leader and Temple pools beside the unit pool), so never count their bodies' Pop as unit population.
- **Fog of war** (no pattern): enemies show only near your own units and buildings, and explored ground you no longer watch turns grey (manual, PDF page 6). Sight bands come from the data's LOS (the registry's sight_reference).
- **Cloaking and detection** (not game-wide): only the Arbiter (Ghastly Vision, a permanent cloak) and the Elite Honor Guard (its Cloak upgrade) can cloak (Active camouflage page; Covenant Temple and Covenant Citadel pages). No page or data flag read names a detector: give no unit the detector trait unless its own page does.
- **Rams** (not game-wide): the Warthog's Ram, the Brute Chopper's run-over and the Ghost's Boosted Ram (an upgrade) are those units' own specials (manual), sharing one ram damage type in the data. No page read says tanks run over infantry by themselves: give no unit `crush` from this note.
- **Stuns, freezing and EMP** (no pattern for the game): they come from named sources only (Cryo Bomb, the Gremlin's EMP, the Flash Bang upgrade, the Vampire's Stasis, the Brutes' Electric Shot upgrade, the Chieftain's hammer upgrades) and belong to them. The data marks which units each can touch (object types such as CanCryo, CanBeFlashBanged and EmpEffectNormal): use that in matchups, citing the data.
- **Base features** (leave off): base turrets and their upgrades, Covenant shield generators, the lockdown and self-destruct of a fully upgraded base (Firebase and Covenant Citadel pages), recycling buildings, and sending supplies to an ally at a loss (Halo Nation's Supplies page).
- **Game modes and skulls** (leave off): bands use the Standard mode, which starts at tech level 0 with 800 supplies (Halo Nation's Standard page). Deathmatch starts with everything researched, and the Strategic Options modes (Keepaway, Tug of War, Reinforcements) change a match's rules (manual, PDF page 9; Halo Nation's Deathmatch page; Strategic Options Pack page). Skulls found in the campaign can be switched on in skirmish too (Halo Wars page, Collectibles).
- **Neutral units** (not researched): rebels, Forerunner Sentinels and, on the map Release, the Flood guard or contest map structures (Rebel Infantry, Rebel base, Forerunner secondary reactor and Forerunner Relic pages). They are not sides: name them only in matchups.
hw1.research_notes:
### Halo Wars (`hw1`)

- **Version.** Code what the registry's version_researched names: the Definitive Edition in Standard mode, whose game data keeps the balance of Title Updates 2 to 4 (its balance techs match Halopedia's Halo Wars Title Updates page, which copies the patch notes). Two gaps stay open: Title Update 6, which the Halo Wars page names, has no notes in any page read, and no page read covers the patches of the Windows 10 and Xbox One builds. Add an uncertain entry where either could change a value.
- **Sites to cite**, with the batch's site test of 11 November:
  - www.halopedia.org: passed 5 of 5 on https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Vehicle_Depot and on https://www.halopedia.org/XRP12_Gremlin. Read it through https://www.halopedia.org/api.php. The building tables use templates (HWResources, HWTech, HWPop) whose icons the rendered page shows: the figure is the number after the icon.
  - halo.fandom.com (Halo Nation): passed 5 of 5 on https://halo.fandom.com/wiki/Standard_(Halo_Wars), the wiki's rendered page from its API (the browser gets 403). Read it through https://halo.fandom.com/api.php.
  - news.xbox.com: passed 5 of 5 on https://news.xbox.com/2016/12/01/fight-forge-halo-wars-definitive-edition-dec-20/ (named by the candidates, not yet cited).
  - Steam: the copy-check cannot read the 2017 posts on store.steampowered.com (those addresses open an empty news hub). Cite the news feed https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamNews/GetNewsForApp/v2/?appid=459220&count=100&maxlength=0&format=json instead. Planetary Annihilation's feed passed 5 of 5, but this one is untested: run the plant test on it before the fill, or check its paraphrases by hand.
  - raw.githubusercontent.com (the game data): the plant test cannot run on it, since an XML data file has no line of prose to plant. Cite figures and tag names from it, never prose.
  - halo.wiki.gallery (Halopedia's copies of the manual and the chart): the copy-check cannot read a PDF. Check paraphrases of them by hand (`pdftotext`, then a six-word check).
  - liquipedia.net is not used for Halo Wars.
- **The game data.** Cite it as kind database, with a title that names the file and says it is the Definitive Edition's data copied in the ensemble-assets repository. It is a public copy of the retail files (`root.era`, with `root_update.era` on top), kept by a third-party project that loads the game's data. Use the pinned commit in every address, so a cited page cannot change: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coconutbird/ensemble-assets/1e8ced921a6dd099c4eac0936aa2f737c5d84ae6/save/<file>`. The files:
  - `root.era/data/objects.xml`: one entry per body, with `Velocity`, `LOS`, `DamageType` (the armour category), `Hitpoints`, `Shieldpoints`, `Pop`, `Veterancy`, `MovementType`, its object types and its `Tactics` file;
  - `root.era/data/squads.xml`: one entry per purchase, with its price in `Supplies`, the tech level it needs as a `Power` cost, its bodies and its `RoleTextID`. Entries whose names start with `cpgn_` are campaign versions: ignore them;
  - `root.era/data/tactics/<object>.tactics.xml`: weapons (`WeaponType`, `MaxRange`, damage, area) and actions. File names are lower case (flamemarine and brutechopper in place of flameMarine and bruteChopper), while object names keep their capitals;
  - `root_update.era/data/weapontypes.xml` (the damage table) and `root.era/data/damagetypes.xml` (the target categories);
  - `root.era/data/techs.xml` and `root_update.era/data/techs_update.xml` (upgrades, and the Title Update balance techs). A balance tech can change a unit's figure (the Gremlin's tech level), so check `techs_update.xml` for the unit before banding;
  - `root.era/data/leaders.xml` (each leader's population pools).
  - Object names for the common units all end in `_01`. UNSC infantry starts with `unsc_inf_`: marine, flameMarine, spartan, cyclops and odst. UNSC vehicles start with `unsc_veh_`: warthog, elephant, gremlin, scorpion, grizzly, cobra and wolverine. UNSC aircraft start with `unsc_air_`: hornet, hawk and vulture. Covenant infantry starts with `cov_inf_`: grunt (an Elite, eliteLeader, leads the squad; the Chieftain's squads are the squad bruteGrunt, whose leader body is bruteLeader), jackal, hunter, brute, eliteCommando (the Elite Honor Guard), suicideGrunt, engineer, arbiter, bruteChief and prophet. Covenant vehicles start with `cov_veh_`: ghost, bruteChopper, wraith, locust and scarab. Covenant aircraft start with `cov_air_`: banshee and vampire. So the Marine squad's object is `unsc_inf_marine_01`.
  - **Super units.** The ODST, Hawk and Grizzly squads in `squads.xml` list the base unit's bodies (Marines, the Hornet, the Scorpion); the super upgrade swaps them (TransformProtoUnit and TransformProtoSquad in `techs.xml`). Read the super unit's own object (`unsc_inf_odst_01` for the ODST, and the Hawk's and the Grizzly's in the same way). The Hawk's laser has WeaponType Missile, so the damage map makes it armour-piercing.
  - **Reading cost.** `objects.xml` (about 1.4 MB) and `techs.xml` (about 0.4 MB) are too big to read whole: search them for the object name and read that entry only. A tactics file is a few kilobytes.
- **When the data and a wiki disagree,** follow the data for the version researched and add an uncertain entry marked sources_disagree that names the wiki page (the rule R1 set for Red Alert's rules copy). Known cases:
  - the Brute Chopper costs 200 in the data and 100 on the Covenant Factory table;
  - the Engineer needs no tech level in the data, the manual and the chart, but 1 on the Covenant Summit table;
  - the Cobra needs tech 3 in the data, the manual, the chart and the Vehicle Depot table, but 2 on the SP42 Cobra page;
  - the Grizzly and Hawk upgrades need tech 4 in the data, the chart and the John Forge and Ellen Anders Gameplay pages, but 3 on the Vehicle Depot and Airpad tables;
  - a Marine squad has four soldiers in the data and five on the official site's page;
  - the official site arms the Spartan with a rifle, the data with an SMG.
  - Official text written in 2009 still decides role words and matchups.
- **Grunt speed.** Grunts move exactly as fast as Marines in the data (same `Velocity` and acceleration), but the manual and the rollover text call them slow. Band from the data figure and add an uncertain entry marked sources_disagree. Nothing read shows whether a squad moves at its bodies' `Velocity` in the engine.
- **Figures in the data.** Speed: `Velocity` divided by the Marines' 10 (speed_raw). Sight: every unit read has an LOS from 55 to 80, so every sight band is medium (long needs more than 82.5), and scout can never rest on long sight. Range: the reference is the Marines' rifle, 25; ignore the in-cover weapons. Many vehicle weapons reach past their own unit's LOS (the Scorpion's cannon reaches 65 with LOS 55, the Wraith's mortar 70, machine guns of 60 on several vehicles), so range bands will often come out off-screen by the rule's first reason. Code it as the rule says, and report it as a rule problem if it looks wrong.
  - The Wraith's main gun is a plasma mortar that reaches far past its sight: whether it is lobbed decides roles step 3 (siege) before step 4 reads the triangle. Decide its delivery from the weapon's own sources.
- **Squads.** Halo Wars sells squads too, so decision 7B applies as for Halo Wars 2: record the squad size in notes. Body counts come from `squads.xml`: Marines 4 (New Blood adds one, the Medic another), Flamethrowers 2, Jackals 2, Hunters 2 (a bonded pair), Brutes 2, Suicide Grunts 4, Grunt squads one leader and 3 Grunts (Peons adds one more, although the manual says two). Each body has its own `Pop`, and a squad takes their sum (four Marines at a quarter each take 1), except the Spartan and the Covenant leaders, whose own pools leave unit population alone (see Population and caps).
- **Weapons in the data.** One tactics file holds every weapon a unit can use, those its upgrades and specials unlock included. A listed weapon can stay switched off until an upgrade turns it on (an ActionEnable effect in `techs.xml`): the Warthog's machine gun waits for Gunner and the Brute Chopper's plasma cannon for Autocannons, so both start armed only with their ram (the official site and the HW:Brute Chieftain page agree). Check `techs.xml` before coding a listed weapon as stock.
  - The Y special is usually its own weapon there (the Marines' grenade, the Scorpion's canister shell, the Vulture's barrage, the Gremlin's EMP): it is an ability, not a weapon (Weapons vs abilities). Upgrade weapons (the Warthog's machine gun and Gauss cannon, the Hornet's Wingmen, the Jackal's beam rifle) are acquired weapons.
  - A weapon's `TargetPriority` list hints at what it engages (the Scorpion's machine gun lists flying units, its cannon does not), but no page says it is the full list of what it can hit: use it as support, beside a page.
- **The flying Engineer.** `cov_inf_engineer_01` has MovementType Air and the object types Aircraft and Flying, and the Summit, the aircraft building, trains it (manual, PDF page 20). Its DamageType is Light, so the armour map's Light to unarmoured meets a flier here: weigh it with the class rules and the soldier rule, and say which decided in armour.notes.
- **Halopedia pages for units.** Halopedia's Halo Wars facts on a unit are spread over the In-game information sections of lore pages (M808B Scorpion, SP42 Cobra, Type-25 Wraith) and over Gameplay subpages that cover several games (Sangheili Honor Guardsman/Gameplay, Type-26 Banshee/Gameplay, Kig-Yar/Gameplay); many units have little there. The building tables (under Official role lines) are the best per-unit source; the leader pages are James Cutter/Gameplay, John Forge/Gameplay, Ellen Anders/Gameplay, The Arbiter (leader) and HW:Brute Chieftain. Some Halopedia text sits in hidden comments, which readers never see: the Halo Wars page's old unit list (the Spartan's shield and SMGs, the Flood on Release) is one. The page reader marks them; never rest a code on commented-out text.
- **Leaders as subfactions.** The registry lists the six leaders as subfactions of `unsc` or `covenant`. A unit every leader of a side fields belongs to the side. A unit only some leaders field belongs to the most general faction that fields it: when two of three do (the Ghost, which the Arbiter and the Prophet field while the Chieftain fields the Brute Chopper instead), record it under the side and say in tier.basis which leader lacks it (the rule R1 used for Red Alert 2's Attack Dog). A unit of one leader goes under that leader (`hw1.cutter.elephant`), the Covenant leaders included (`hw1.arbiter.arbiter`). A leader's changed version of a side's unit (the Chieftain's Brute-led Grunt squad) is its own entry under that leader with variant_of, if the trim keeps it.
- **Lineage.** Halo Wars is the earliest game in the registry for the Halo lines, so a design that Halo Wars 2 also has takes its `hw1` slug as its lineage id (the Ids rule).
- **Armour map steps** (armour-class step 1 lets these notes name a step): the Warthog, the Gremlin and the Brute Chopper take one step down, from the map's medium to light. The manual calls the Warthog and the Gremlin lightly armoured, the Chopper is a bike (our light class names motorbikes), and in the data all three have well under half the Cobra's health. Shielded is left out of the map because the data gives it to infantry, vehicles and a leader alike, with no shield on some of them as bought (the Wraith, the Ghost, the Elite Honor Guard): those units go on to steps 2 to 5 (the Wraith, a cost-anchor tank, is heavy by step 3).
- **Patterns to look for**, beyond the registry entry's teaches_patterns: `self-destruct` (Suicide Grunts; the Banshee's Sacrifice upgrade), `pull-target` (the Chieftain's Birthright upgrade and Vortex), `retaliate-on-hit` (the Arbiter's Fiendish Return), `overclock-self` (the Arbiter's Rage, paid in supplies per second), `bombard-area` (the Prophet's Cleansing beam), `repair-allies` (the Engineer; the Cyclops after its Repair Kit), `cloak` (the Elite Honor Guard), `leap` (the Brutes' Jump Pack), `lock-in-stasis` or `disable-machine` for the Vampire's Stasis (it holds aircraft and, with its upgrade, drains them, so check which summary fits), `leave-hazard-zone` (the Wraith's Scorch), the Hornet's Chaff Pod (a passive upgrade that turns missiles aside: weigh `fire-countermeasures`, which is on a key, against the interceptor armour model, which works by itself) and `launch-drones` (the Prophet's two Protector Sentinels, an upgrade).

cost_thresholds.basis: Price = supplies, the only resource a unit costs; the tech level and population room it needs are not spent. Anchor: the two main battle tanks, both with the role line Main Vehicle: the UNSC Scorpion (500) and the Covenant Wraith (350); the mean is 425. Thresholds at 0.5, 0.9, 1.4 and 2 times the anchor, rounded to the nearest 10. The Wraith is far cheaper than the Scorpion, so it falls in low and the Scorpion in medium. A super unit (ODSTs, Grizzly, Hawk) costs what its base unit costs, since the upgrade that unlocks it is bought for every unit of the type. A Covenant leader's price is the 400 paid to bring it back; the first comes free with the Temple. Leader-power prices and the Covenant leaders' running cost per second are not unit prices.

value.speed_reference: Marines (the UNSC main infantry squad, four soldiers, trained at the Barracks). In the Definitive Edition's game data (objects.xml) each Marine has Velocity 10; the manual and Halopedia give no speeds. Ratio = the unit's Velocity / 10, both from that data. Whether the engine moves a squad at exactly this figure was not checked (Grunts have the same figure, but official text calls them slow).
value.sight_reference: Marines: LOS 55 in the Definitive Edition's game data (objects.xml), how far a unit clears the fog of war; the game shows no sight figure and Halopedia gives none. Every unit read has an LOS from 55 to 80, so every sight band comes out medium.
value.range_reference: The Marines' assault rifle: MaxRange 25 in its tactics file (unsc_inf_marine_01.tactics in the Definitive Edition's game data). open_questions: HW1-LEADERS: should Halo Wars' six leaders be subfactions? The question: the drafted registry entry lists Sergeant Forge, Captain Cutter, Professor Anders, the Arbiter, the Brute Chieftain and the Prophet of Regret as subfactions of the UNSC and the Covenant (as Red Alert 2's countries and Generals' generals are), while Halo Wars 2 keeps two factions and names its leaders in notes. Why it matters: it sets the unit ids and factions for the whole hw1 batch (hw1.cutter.elephant or hw1.unsc.elephant). Options: (A) subfactions, as drafted: each leader fields units the others lack (Elephant and ODSTs; Cyclops and Grizzly; Gremlin and Hawk; Suicide Grunts; Brutes and the Brute Chopper; Elite Honor Guard), the three Covenant leaders are units themselves, the Chieftain's Grunt squads differ, and Halopedia calls the leaders sub-factions; the candidate list's ids then move to the leaders (hw1.anders.gremlin, hw1.arbiter.arbiter). (B) two factions, as Halo Wars 2: leaders named in notes and tier.basis, ids stay as the candidate list has them, and the six leader entries, the research notes' subfaction bullet and the Temple gate's tag become simpler. Recommendation: A. Halo Wars has only six fixed leaders, each with its own units, and three of them fight as units; Halo Wars 2 stays two factions because its sixteen leaders mostly swap one or two units.

### Halo Wars 2 (`hw2`)

Written in the batch R4 preparation, before any `hw2` unit is coded, from Halopedia's ten Halo Wars 2 building pages, a sample of its unit pages, its Halo Wars 2, Phoenix Logs and Season 0 to 15 pages and two heroes' gameplay pages, and Halo Alpha's Wraith, Banshee, Ghost and Phantom pages; checked by a second researcher.

- **Where official text is.** No Halo Wars 2 manual was found (Halopedia has a manual page only for Halo Wars), and Halo Waypoint's Halo Wars 2 game page answers HTTP 500. Official text comes from three places: the in-game production tooltip, the Phoenix Logs (the in-game codex) and the patch notes.
- **The production tooltip** ([Halo Wars 2](https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars_2), Gameplay, Units) gives each unit a type line that names its own job (in place of the Killer labels of Halo Wars), a description of a few short phrases, and four counter icons. Halopedia copies the first two in two places: the Type and Description columns of the table on each building page, and the Info line in the Halo Wars 2 part of most unit pages, which usually includes the type. Neither says what it copies, but the building pages credit their quote boxes to the in-game description, the Foundry table marks a slip in the Marauder's text with [sic], and Halo Alpha quotes the same phrases for the Wraith and the Ghost. Read both as copies of in-game text, with two cautions.
  - **Dates differ.** Halo Alpha's blocks mostly show beta or launch text and prices. Halopedia's tables and unit pages each mix dates (the Wolverine and Reaver pages carry the April 2018 prices, while the Foundry's Reaver row matches no listed change), so check every value from either against the Season pages (research notes, Prices). The Ghost is fast moving in the Banished outpost table but very fast moving in Halo Alpha's quote.
  - **Copy errors in the Type column.** The Scorpion and the Warthog's Gauss Cannon upgrade are typed Core Aircraft ([UNSC Garage](https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Garage)). The Chopper is typed Light Infantry with a price of nothing ([Banished outpost](https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_outpost)); both look like Cannon Fodder's values, since its description opens with Light Infantry and calls it free. The Chopper's last listed price is 245 + 15 (Season 1).
- **Roles step 1: the type line is the designation.** Read the Type cell of the unit's row on its building page, and check it against the type in the unit page's Info line and, where one exists, Halo Alpha's Purpose line. A role counts when every copy that names a role names the same one; skip a cell that is a plain copy error. Every unit has a type line, so step 1 never falls back to the description.
  - Type words that name a role: Anti-Infantry gives anti-infantry. Anti-Vehicle Mech or plain Anti-Vehicle gives anti-armour, through the alias anti-vehicle; Anti-Air, Anti-Air Vehicle or Anti-Air Mech gives anti-air; Mobile Artillery gives siege, through the alias artillery, and siege's coding rule still applies; Scout, Scout Vehicle or Scout Mech gives scout; Support Unit gives support only when the stock unit meets support's requires (the Nightingale and the Banished Engineer heal and repair; the Shroud, the Frostraven and the Methane Wagon do neither, so step 1 skips support for them).
  - Words that name no role: Core Infantry, Core Vehicle, Core Aircraft, Core Air, Core Mech, Core Tank, Main Battle Tank, Heavy Tank, Heavy Mech, Heavy Air, Light Infantry, Mobile Garrison, Super Unit, Hero Infantry, Hero Vehicle, Hero Mech and Hero Unit. Anti-Building (Jump Pack Brutes, Elite Enforcers, Grunt Riders) and Anti-Building Mech (Locust) name none either: anti-building is not a label or alias of siege in the word list. By their rows the first three are close-range rushers and the Locust fires a beam straight at its target, so siege's coding rule fits none of them and the later steps decide; add a fit_note at roles that names the anti-building job, for the rule-fix round.
  - Names: the Sniper's name names its job, so official text calls it a sniper: marksman at roles.secondary step 1, but only if its weapon is of the sniper family and reaches long, as marksman's coding rule asks. The Banished Engineer is a Huragok that heals and repairs; its name names the engineer role only if it builds or takes over structures, and the Apex table says neither.
- **Descriptions, patch notes and Phoenix Logs** count for roles.secondary step 1 and for strong and weak wording.
  - A description phrase that names a job counts: each Mobile Garrison can transport infantry (transport, whose two-seat rule still applies).
  - The patch notes on Halopedia's Season pages copy the official Halo Waypoint forum posts, each one cited there. They often name a unit's job: [Season 6](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_6_(Halo_Wars_2)) groups the Cyclops and the Hunters as anti-vehicle units, and says its fix lets the Reaver work as an anti-air unit; [Season 9](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_9_(Halo_Wars_2)) (8 February 2018, Global) wants core air, the tech-2 Hornet and Banshee, to be one of an army's anti-vehicle answers; [Season 10](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_10_(Halo_Wars_2)) treats Wolverines and Reavers as AA and wants scouts to beat rush infantry and lose to core infantry; [Season 11](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_11_(Halo_Wars_2)) calls the Elite Rangers an anti-infantry unit of tier 2 and gives Voridus's Brute Grenadiers a weapon type that makes them real anti-infantry.
  - [Phoenix Logs](https://www.halopedia.org/Phoenix_Logs) says its entries are copied word for word from the game, and each unit page draws in the unit's entry. An entry opens with a short line (the Wraith's: heavy mortar tank) and then tells the machine's story. It is official text, but not the designation. The Wraith's entry has it serve as a mainline tank and as artillery, so official text names siege, through the alias artillery, for the Wraith at roles.secondary step 1 (siege's coding rule still applies). The infobox role field that cites a log only restates it: read the log.
- **Strong against and weak against.** The tooltip has no Strong vs. or Weak vs. line. Its four icons grade the unit against infantry, vehicles, aircraft and buildings: green for good, yellow for okay, red for poor and none for a kind it cannot attack ([Halo Wars 2](https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars_2), Units). Pages report the grades in words: Halopedia's unit-page prose uses the same scale (does well or is effective, okay, poor, cannot attack), and so do the heroes' own gameplay pages ([Jerome-092/Gameplay](https://www.halopedia.org/Jerome-092/Gameplay), [Pavium/Gameplay](https://www.halopedia.org/Pavium/Gameplay)); Halo Alpha's Attack Strength list uses Good, Moderate and Poor or Weak. Read a good grade as official strong-against text for roles step 4, and a poor grade as a weak point for the roles.secondary drop rule, only when a page gives the grade for that unit on that scale; cite the page. Okay and Moderate are neither. When two reports disagree, use neither and add an uncertain entry with sources_disagree. A few descriptions have wording of their own: the Reaver page's Info line calls it weak against vehicles. Wording on an upgrade or an ability (Canister Shell strong against infantry, Scorch Mortar strong against ground targets, Plasma Torpedo much stronger against aircraft) belongs to that part only and never counts at roles step 4 for the stock unit.
- **Game data bonus (roles step 4).** The patch notes give some damage modifiers from the game data: core air (the Hornet and the Banshee) against tier 3 tanks and the Colossus at 1.3 since 2 April 2018 (Season 10, Global), and the Jackrabbit against scouts at 1.7 since 18 July 2018 (Season 11). Count a modifier above 1.0 only when a note gives its value for the unit's current main weapon and no later note changes it; a change given only in per cent does not show a value above 1.0.
