### Halo Wars 2 (`hw2`)

Written in the batch R4 preparation, before any `hw2` unit is coded, from Halopedia's Halo Wars 2 page (Gameplay), its ten building pages, its Resources, Garrison, Power Node, Leader power, Leader, Active camouflage, Red Team, Phoenix Logs and Season 0 to 15 pages, and the gameplay pages of Captain Cutter, Jerome-092, Colony and Pavium; checked by a second researcher. Standard skirmish and multiplayer only: Blitz plays with cards instead of bases and stays out.

- **Basic orders** (no pattern): every unit. Move, attack, attack-move, queued orders, hold position, select all and control groups. Attack-move and hold position came on 26 September 2017 ([Season 7](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_7_(Halo_Wars_2)), Control improvements); queued waypoints are older on PC (the 20 March 2017 notes fix Shift + right-click waypoints). A unit's own special ability on the Y button is not an order: record it on the unit (the patch notes speak of the Wraith's and the Brute Grenadiers' Y abilities, Seasons 1 and 14).
- **Veterancy** (earn-veterancy; leave it off): units earn XP toward three ranks, each rank lifting attack and defence; a Spartan riding a hijacked vehicle can climb to six ([Halo Wars 2](https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars_2), Units). The patch notes speak of the XP each rank needs (raised for heroes in June 2017, [Season 4](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_4_(Halo_Wars_2)); brought in line for Forge's and Pavium's heroes in July 2018, Season 11), but no page read says what earns XP or shows a rank adding a weapon or a button, so no unit links earn-veterancy. A unit with rank bonuses of its own (the Brute Grenadiers' extra damage and protection per rank, Season 15) says so in notes. Leader powers that speed up ranking (Battle Hardened), promote units (Field Promotion, which the Halo Wars 2 page says works on unarmed units too) or drop units that are already ranked are side-wide.
  - The strategy part of Captain Cutter's page says Battle Hardened works for every unit but the Nightingale, which hints that the Nightingale never ranks up: its coder adds an uncertain entry. Voridus's Pack Assault drops a veteran Infused Engineer (Season 8), so an Engineer can hold a rank.
- **Unit upgrades** (Paired entries): the building tables list each unit's upgrades under the building that researches them (rows typed New Ability, Unit Upgrade or Weapon Upgrade). Record what each adds, with source upgrade. No page read says whether an upgrade also reaches units already in the field, so link upgrade-in-field only where a cited page shows that, and otherwise add an uncertain entry at the ability or weapon; the merge pass sets the batch's line.
- **Army and base upgrades** (side-wide; leave them off): Infantry, Vehicle and Air Upgrades I to III (more damage and health for the whole class, at the Barracks or Raid Camp, the Garage or Foundry, the Airpad or Apex), and, at the Armory or War Council, Fortify Base, Advanced Logistics (faster production) and Reinforcements (a higher population cap). Bands use the stock unit.
- **Leader powers and privileges** (side-wide): every leader has ten powers on a radial menu, unlocked one at a time with leader points earned in play ([Leader power](https://www.halopedia.org/Leader_power), Halo Wars 2), and privileges that change whole classes (Cutter's faster infantry, Jerome's stronger units at low population). Leave them off. A power that gives named unit types a new button or effect is recorded on each of them, with source commander-power: UNSC Raid II lets Jackrabbits capture points ([James Cutter/Gameplay](https://www.halopedia.org/James_Cutter/Gameplay); no pattern fits, so add a fit_note, as for de-capture below). A power that only changes numbers (Battle Hardened, Time for Heroes, Recon Sight) is not an ability. A power that adds a death effect (Kinsano's Hellcharge, Season 15) goes in on_death.notes.
- **Units that a leader power brings.** A unit that a leader point unlocks for purchase at the Firebase or Outpost (Protector Sentinel, Mastodon, Frostraven, Skitterer, Phantom, Methane Wagon, Wraith Invader) is a unit of its own: its gate is the tech level in the table, and tier.basis names the power. A unit that only a power drops onto the field (ODSTs from ODST Drop, Omega Team, Decimus from Decimus Drop, the Retriever Sentinel, the Pelicans of Close Air Support, the Lich of Lich Vanguard) is a call-in with no gate in the tier_map: leave it out unless the trim and the registry add one.
- **Capturing points** (no pattern; leave it off): only infantry take a Forerunner Power Node, once its Sentinel guards are dead, and the node then yields power ([Power Node](https://www.halopedia.org/Power_Node), Halo Wars 2). capture-structure does not fit, since the nodes are neutral. Units whose description calls them quick capture units (Marines, Grunt Squad, Heavy Grunts, Cannon Fodder) say so in strengths. Turning an enemy-held point back to neutral (Can de-capture, on the Jackrabbit and the Chopper) is not game-wide: record it on those units with a fit_note, as no registered pattern fits.
- **Garrison towers** (carry-passengers on the building; leave it off the units): most multiplayer maps have Forerunner Garrison towers that hold one infantry unit, giving it cover and more range and sight ([Garrison](https://www.halopedia.org/Garrison)). Entering and leaving are universal keys; range and sight bands use the unit outside.
- **Mobile Garrisons** (Paired entries): the Mastodon, Phantom and Wraith Invader carry infantry that fire from inside (their table rows), so each keeps one seat passive linking passenger-sets-weapon. Loading and unloading are universal keys. Seat counts come from the rows: the Mastodon three, four with Infantry Capacity; the Phantom two, three with Gunboat Capacity; the Wraith Invader's row gives no count.
- **Hijacking and commandeering**: not game-wide. Only the three classic Spartan heroes do it (Jerome-092 for Cutter, Alice-130 for Isabel, Douglas-042 for Anders), through their Hijack upgrade, which takes enemy vehicles and aircraft and boards friendly ones ([UNSC Armory](https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Armory)); Commander Jerome cannot ([Jerome-092/Gameplay](https://www.halopedia.org/Jerome-092/Gameplay)). Record it on the three: hijack-vehicle for the enemy side; for boarding a friendly vehicle, test join-ally-crew's summary. The Omega Team call-in hijacks too, but call-ins are left out.
- **Cloak and detection**: a cloaked unit cannot be targeted until a detector reveals it ([Active camouflage](https://www.halopedia.org/Active_camouflage), Halo Wars 2). Cloaking belongs to the unit that does it: the Active Camo upgrades of the Sniper and of the Shipmaster's and Arbiter's Grunts, the Honor Guard, and the Shroud's field (the cloak pattern, on each). A unit hidden only by a Shroud, a Cloaking Generator or a leader power gets no cloak. Detection is the sensor trait detector on each unit whose description says it detects cloaked units (Sniper, Wolverine, Nightingale, Reaver, Elite Rangers, Banished Engineer); the Jackrabbit, Chopper and Ghost detect only after an upgrade, so put that in sensors.notes. Since 2 April 2018 a detector reveals cloaked units out to its base line of sight, whatever the high ground ([Season 10](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_10_(Halo_Wars_2)), Global). Sensor Towers and Cloaking Generators are buildings.
- **Shields** (armour model regen-shield, per unit): some units carry an energy shield, among them the Wraith from the start (its page) and the Spartans. The Spartans' shields recharge after a pause ([Red Team](https://www.halopedia.org/Red_Team), Changes from Halo Wars; their Phoenix Log entries say so too), and Commander Jerome's Info line has a fast-recharging shield; no page read says so for vehicle shields. Code regen-shield on a unit whose own sources give it a stock shield, with an uncertain entry at armour/models when no page shows that shield recharging; a shield that only an upgrade adds goes in armour.notes. Base shields belong to buildings.
- **Healing** (none game-wide): units do not heal by themselves; the Marines lost their healing out of combat ([UNSC Marine Corps/Gameplay](https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Marine_Corps/Gameplay), Changes). Units that heal or repair others record repair-allies (Nightingale, Banished Engineer, the Marines' Combat Tech upgrade); Pavium's row says he repairs structures, so test repair-allies against his own pages. Healing leader powers (Restoration Drones, Atriox's Bulwark, Colony's Engineer Swarm and Combat Repair) are side-wide. Code self-repair only where a unit's own stock sources show it healing itself; healing that an upgrade adds (Cannon Fodder's Refer a Friend, the Jackrabbit's Support Drone) goes in notes.
- **Population** (side-wide; no pattern): units take population, from a cap of 80 that the Armory or War Council raises to 120 ([Resources](https://www.halopedia.org/Resources), Halo Wars 2); heroes take none (their table rows).
- **Heroes** (availability unique): each leader has one hero, bought at the Armory or War Council at tech 1 (most for 300 supplies and 275 power), with a limit of one active hero ([Jerome-092/Gameplay](https://www.halopedia.org/Jerome-092/Gameplay), the Spartan's Info line). In multiplayer a dead hero is bought again, never revived ([Red Team](https://www.halopedia.org/Red_Team)). Tech 1 maps to t1 and unique starts at t2, so each hero keeps its t1 and records the atypical entry 'availability:unique min_tier t2', as games-r3.md does for Iron Harvest's heroes. Each hero upgrade raises health and damage and adds one ability or weapon: record the added part with source upgrade, and put the health and damage in notes.
- **Super units** (availability open unless a page shows a cap of their own): the UNSC Condor and the Banished Scarab (the Volatile Scarab for Voridus) cost 2,000 supplies, 2,000 power and 40 population at tech 3. The Scarab page allows up to three at once in standard modes, which is also all that the top population cap leaves room for; add an uncertain entry at availability.
- **Ramming**: not game-wide. A unit whose description or patch notes show a ram (Warthog, Flame Warthog, Ghost, Grunt Riders; the Chopper in Seasons 4, 10 and 15) records it on itself. The rams of Choppers, Ghosts and Warthogs, and the Scarab's stomp, share one damage type, and a rammer takes back part of the damage it deals ([Season 10](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_10_(Halo_Wars_2)), Global).
- **Crates** (picking one up is a universal key): supply and power crates lie on the map for units to collect ([Resources](https://www.halopedia.org/Resources)). Leave them off; a unit that gathers faster says so in strengths (Grunt squads gather faster since Season 2).
- **Sight** (no pattern): fog of war covers the map, and high ground raises a unit's line of sight but not its detection range (Season 10, Global). Sight bands use flat ground.
- **Squads** (crew model squad): infantry are sold as squads (Marines come four to a squad). Upgrades that only add members (Pack Brother, Dark Skies, New "Recruits", Squad Reserves, Arbiter's Champion) change numbers: notes. An added member with a weapon or job of its own (the Marines' Combat Tech, with a rocket launcher and repairs) is an upgrade weapon or ability.
- **Base features** (leave off): locking down a Firebase or Outpost to hold trained units inside, turrets and their upgrades, Sensor Towers, Cloaking and Shield Generators.
- **No crushing found**: no page read shows vehicles running over infantry outside a ram; give crush only where a unit's own page shows it.
hw2.research_notes:
### Halo Wars 2 (`hw2`)

Written in the batch R4 preparation (11 November 2026), before any `hw2` unit is coded, and checked by a second researcher. It replaces step 1's Halo Wars 2 bullet in this section, and four step-1 passages that the check showed wrong in part: the Halo Wars 2 bullet under Tiers that were hard to map, the Halo Wars 2 price bullet, the HW2 speed bullet and item 1 under Uncertain. Their right parts are kept below, word for word where possible.

- **Sites** (replaces step 1's bullet here).
  - Halopedia allows API access and plain page loads: https://www.halopedia.org/api.php.
  - Halo Alpha (halo.fandom.com, kind wiki) answers a plain page request with HTTP 403, so read it through https://halo.fandom.com/api.php. Its blocks hold mostly beta or launch values (Version traps).
  - Halo Waypoint (www.halowaypoint.com) is official. Its old Halo Wars 2 game page and three 2017 posts answered HTTP 500, while the 2021 post https://www.halowaypoint.com/news/lovely-letters read normally.
  - Patch notes are on the Season pages (Season 0 to 15), each of which copies and cites the official Halo Waypoint forum post. Season 15 holds the last two: 13 August 2020, and 4 September 2020, which retuned only Kinsano's Hellcharge.
  - The Prima eGuide (official) is behind Cloudflare.
  - Pages for the copy-check's site test, one per site: https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Garage (a building table, In-game information), https://halo.fandom.com/wiki/Eklon'dal_Workshop_Mortar_Tank and https://www.halowaypoint.com/news/lovely-letters. The test of 11 November flagged every planted passage on all three sites, but on Halo Waypoint only on its news index, so test the Halo Wars 2 post as well.
  - The ten building pages, the sixteen Season pages and the mechanic pages named in this note are in the page cache: reuse them.
- **Cost tables.** They are on the building pages: UNSC Barracks, Garage and Airpad; Banished Raid Camp, Foundry and Apex; Firebase, Banished outpost, UNSC Armory and Banished War Council. Columns: Population, Tech, Supplies, Power. Step 1's Banished Hall and Summit have no Halo Wars 2 page (they are Covenant buildings of Halo Wars). A row may give campaign and skirmish values side by side (the Nightingale: 400 + 0 in the campaign, 350 + 50 in skirmish): use skirmish. Some rows have wrong type labels: the Scorpion is labelled "Core Aircraft" (more under Official role lines).
- **Tiers** (replaces step 1's Halo Wars 2 bullet under Tiers that were hard to map).
  - Halopedia's unit tables give each unit a "Tech" value from 0 to 3. The HQ upgrades unlock tech 1 to 3: Combat Station, Command Center and Headquarters (UNSC); Stronghold, Citadel and Fortress (Banished).
  - Tech 0 and tech 1 are both t1, tech 2 is t2 and tech 3 is t3, because the official patch notes use those tiers: the notes of 7 July 2017 (Season 4) want Jerome's Mantis beatable at tier 1 by scout vehicles or by core infantry with upgrades, units of tech 0 and 1, and compare the heroes, all tech 1, at tier 1; Season 6 names the tech-2 Warthog, Flame Warthog, Mantis and Marauder tier 2 vehicles and the tech-3 Scorpion, Wraith, Colossus and Grizzly tier 3; Season 9 calls the tech-3 Blisterback a tier 3 unit.
  - Whether a match starts at tech 0 or tech 1 is disputed, and no band depends on it. The Banished outpost page says the first base of a match is a Stronghold, and the Banished Apex page says its tech-1 need lets it go up at once; but both base tables sell the first HQ upgrade (Combat Station, Stronghold) for 400 power from tech 0, and the outpost's Phoenix log has the Outpost upgraded into a Stronghold.
  - Exception: the notes of 29 June 2017 ([Season 4](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_4_(Halo_Wars_2))) count the Kodiak among the tier 3 UNSC vehicles, while the Garage table and Halo Alpha put it at tech 2. Code it t2, with an uncertain entry at tier marked sources_disagree.
  - Consequence: the Garage, Airpad and Foundry need tech 2, so Warthogs, Hornets, Wolverines and Marauders are t2, and the Scorpion, Wraith and Vulture are t3. Heroes such as Atriox's Chosen are listed at tech 1, so they are t1.
  - Tech levels to watch: the Cyclops, Hunters and Elite Rangers need tech 2 although their buildings are open from the start (t2). The Banished Apex needs tech 1 while the UNSC Airpad needs tech 2, so the Banished Engineer is t1 and the Nightingale t2. The Ghost is tech 1, though the Chopper it replaces is tech 0.
  - Unit upgrades (Gauss Warthog, Canister Shell) are upgrades, not tiers.
  - The Flood appear only as enemies (Awakening the Nightmare campaign, Terminus Firefight). They are not a playable side; skip them or mark them atypical. A Flood unit would rest on campaign or Firefight values, outside version_researched's skirmish and multiplayer scope, so the trim should leave it out or say so.
- **Prices** (replaces step 1's Halo Wars 2 price bullet): supplies + power at par, anchor about 630 (Scorpion 550 + 90, Wraith 550 + 75); thresholds 320, 570, 880 and 1,260, worked out from the rounded anchor of 630 (step 1 gave 890 and 1,270, from the mean of 632.5).
  - Very low: Marines 150, Jackrabbit 212, Warthog 250, Hornet 300, Grunt Goblin 310.
  - Low: Wolverine 330, Nightingale 400, Kodiak 525.
  - Medium: most heroes 575 (Pavium 625), Scorpion 640, Vulture 850, Colossus 870.
  - High: Grizzly 990.
  - Very high: Scarab 4,000.
  - Uncertain: no source gives supply income rates (the patch notes give only the power income of the map's Energy Capture Points), so power is not weighted. The Halopedia tables are not tied to a patch. A search snippet of the Prima eGuide (the official guide, behind Cloudflare, so I could not open it) suggested a launch Scorpion price of about 650 resources. Leader-power drops and Blitz card costs are not unit prices.
  - The anchor's Wraith price is in doubt (registry basis). With its last listed price, 525 + 70, the thresholds would be 310, 560, 870 and 1,240, so a unit priced where the two sets differ (310 to 319, 560 to 569, 870 to 879, 1,240 to 1,259) adds an uncertain entry at cost_band: the Colossus (870), the Phantom (315) and the Grunt Goblin (310).
- **Reading a price** (cost_band.raw). Halopedia's tables and unit pages are not kept to one patch: many rows match the last price change on the Season pages, but some keep an older price or match no listed change. Take the price from the newest patch note that changes it, reading the Season pages newest first; take none from Halo Alpha.
  - One exception: when the building table and the unit's own page agree on a price that no note gives, it may be a later change the notes leave out: keep it, and give the last listed price in an uncertain entry marked sources_disagree. This holds for the Wraith (550 + 75 on both, where the last note, of 20 March 2017, set 525 + 70), which keeps raw in line with the registry's anchor, and for the Shroud (400 + 60 on both; Season 6 cut it from 550 to 450).
  - Where the table and the page differ, the one that matches the newest note wins: the Reaver's page has 175 + 215, as the April 2018 notes do, while its row has 175 + 210.
  - Rows known to be stale or wrong: the Jackrabbit (220 + 15 on the table and its page, from 7 March 2017; 200 + 12 since 20 March 2017), the Cyclops (row 120 + 150; 120 + 120 since March 2017, as its page has), the Chopper (row 0 + 0; 245 + 15 since March 2017) and Cannon Fodder (row 100 supplies, but its description calls it free and the Halo Wars 2 page says Yapyap recruits it without spending resources: raw 0, with the row's figure in an uncertain entry). Commander Jerome costs 300 + 275 on the Armory table and 350 + 250 on his gameplay page (Season 11 brought the heroes of Forge, Voridus and the Arbiter from 350 + 275 down to 300 + 275; Pavium's row still has 350 + 275). The Hunters', Elite Rangers' and Suicide Grunts' rows split supplies and power unlike the last note but give the same sum, so raw does not change.
- **Speed** (replaces step 1's HW2 speed bullet). The registry's speed_reference reads the description's speed word as the band of the same name, which the speed-bands rule allows only where the registry says so. Some patch notes give speeds (the Season 14 notes on Halopedia raise the Vulture from 9 to 11), but there is no Marine figure to divide by.
  - The other figures on that scale: Banshee 20.5 (2 April 2018, given as a yardstick in the Cleansing Beam note), the classic Spartan heroes 15 (17 August 2017), Hunters 12 and Shroud 11 (8 February 2018), Jump Pack Brutes 11 (18 April 2019). The Hornet was raised to the Wolverine's speed (8 February 2018) and Commander Jerome lost a quarter of his base speed (13 August 2020), with no figure. Use them to judge a unit with no word, with an uncertain entry at mobility/speed.
  - Words: Fast moving is misspelt Fast moiving in the Garage table (Warthog, Flame Warthog); Slow and Tough (Pavium) counts as slow. The Cyclops has fast moving only in its page's older Info line, and no speed word in the Barracks row, and no note changes its speed: take fast, with an uncertain entry that names both. Where two copies give different words (the Ghost: fast moving in the outpost table, very fast moving in Halo Alpha), take the band nearer medium and mark the uncertain entry sources_disagree.
- **Sight.** The registry's sight_reference gives the detectors' base line of sight of April 2018; with no Marine figure every sight band is still a medium proposal. The Jackrabbit's figure predates 18 July 2018, when its extra sight moved onto the Support Drone (Season 11).
- **Range words.** The descriptions grade reach in words: Very long range (Sniper, Kodiak, Blisterback), Long range (Elite Rangers, Locust, Wraith, Colossus), Medium range (Scorpion, Grizzly, Hornet, Banshee) and Mid-range missiles (Wolverine, Reaver). The patch notes give reach changes only in per cent, so the range tie-break takes the band the source names: long for long or very long, medium for medium or mid-range.
- **Armour class, step 2** (the game's own armour word).
  - Read the patch notes' named groups first. Season 6 counts the Warthog, Flame Warthog, Mantis and Marauder as Medium units and the Scorpion, Wraith, Colossus and Grizzly as Heavy units. Season 10 (2 April 2018) lists its light armored units (in its words: Flamers, Cryo Flamers, Suicide Grunt, Brute Rider and Brute Grenadier); Brute Rider is no table name, so match it with an uncertain entry.
  - Otherwise the description's armour word decides when it is light or heavy, with very or a word form ignored: Light armor (Sniper, Jackrabbit, Chopper, Ghost, Wolverine, Reaver, Locust), Very light armor (Skitterer), Heavy armor (Cyclops, Scorpion, spelt Hevay in the Garage table, Grizzly, Wraith, Vulture, Blisterback, Hunter Captain), Heavily armored (Hunters), Very heavy armor (Condor, Scarab; check A then applies). Tough armor (Marauder, Mantis) and Tougher Grunts (Heavy Grunts) are not class words.
  - Step 2 reads only a bare light, medium or heavy. A patch-note class that joins the word to a kind of unit, written as one word or two, is not an armour word: Light Infantry, LightRush, HeavyInfantry, MediumAA, MediumHero, MediumScout. So Cannon Fodder, whose description opens with Light Infantry, goes on to the soldier rule.
  - The soldier rule's game data: on 20 March 2017 (Season 1) the Elite Rangers got an armour type that resists the small arms of Marine and Grunt squads better, a tougher infantry armour type, so they are light.
  - No armour_map: no page gives every unit's type.
- **Leader units.** Faction unsc or banished, no subfactions. A leader's unit with its own in-game name is a unit of its own (Grizzly, Mantis, Colossus, Flame Warthog, Cryo Troopers, Elite Enforcers, Grunt Riders, Heavy Grunts, Cannon Fodder, the Ghost of the Shipmaster and the Arbiter, the Volatile Scarab and the leader-power units). Name the leader, and the standard unit it replaces, in tier.basis; availability stays open. Set variant_of only when a source names a standard unit as its base (the Flame Warthog to the Warthog; the Volatile Scarab to the Scarab, whose page covers both); a unit that only replaces another (the Grizzly for the Scorpion) gets none. A unit that keeps its standard name under every leader (the Grunt Squad, which the Shipmaster and the Arbiter lead with an Elite and other upgrades) is one unit, with the leader's version in notes. The units of Pavium and Voridus get introduced_in hw2-awakening-the-nightmare (the expansion's page says it added both leaders); the other leaders added after launch as downloadable content belong to no registered expansion and get none.
- **Page names.** In-game names are short (Wraith, Cyclops); page titles are lore names: Eklon'Dal_Workshop_Wraith, HRUNTING_Mark_III_(S)_Cyclops, M9_Wolverine, Dovotaa_Workshop_Reaver, M121_Jackrabbit, Barukaza_Workshop_Scarab, G81_Condor. Follow the link in the Name cell of the building table. The Marines and Grunt Squad rows have no link: use UNSC_Marine_Corps/Gameplay for the Marines, and find the Grunts' page through the API. Ids follow the Name cell (Grunt Squad gives grunt; Jump Pack Brutes gives jump-pack-brutes).
- **Version traps.** The Halo Wars 2 part of a unit page can show older values: the Jackrabbit page lists a weapon upgrade that the June 2017 patch made standard, and the Cyclops page has the March 2017 price. Halo Alpha's blocks are mostly beta or launch (Scorpion 390 + 120, Reaver 235 + 100, Banshee at tech 1; its Ghost block is headed Banshee). Check every value against the Season pages, newest first.
- **Matchups in official words** (for counters and countered_by). The patch notes state intended matchups: scouts beat rush infantry and lose to core infantry such as Marines and Grunts (Season 10); infantry are meant to answer aircraft (Season 9 on the Elite Rangers; Season 10 raises the Marines' and Grunts' damage against air); aircraft are meant to answer vehicles (Season 9, 8 February 2018; Season 10 trims that bonus against tier 3 tanks); the Cyclops and Hunters counter the tier 2 vehicles (Season 6); and Season 15 cut the Wraith's damage against anti-vehicle units, which it had been beating.
- **Lineage.** Halo Wars (`hw1`) is in this batch, so check each unit against it: the same name and the same job (the Warthog, Scorpion, Wolverine, Hornet, Wraith, Ghost and Banshee, among others) gives the Halo Wars slug as lineage. Halopedia's UNSC Barracks page links the Halo Wars Flamethrower row to its Hellbringers page, so those two share one as well.
- **Sentinels.** The Aggressor Sentinels that guard Power Nodes are neutral guards, not a side; Anders's Protector Sentinel and Retriever Sentinel are UNSC units.

### Planetary Annihilation: TITANS (`pa`)

Written in the batch R4 preparation (11 November 2026), before any `pa` unit is coded, and checked by a second researcher. Sources: PA Lobby's TITANS unit pages and their blueprint views, the developers' posts on the game's Steam news feed from April 2022 to October 2026, the Steam store page and the Planetary Annihilation Wiki on Fandom.

- **Official text: the in-game unit description.** Every unit blueprint read has a description string, and the game shows it in the build bar's preview (the hotfix of 21 August 2026 stopped it spilling over the icons there). The blueprints of units other than commanders mark it for translation (`!LOC:`).
  - PA Lobby prints it in italics under the unit's name, on the unit page (palobby.com, /units/unit/<id>?version=titans; the Dox's is https://palobby.com/units/unit/assault_bot?version=titans). The blueprint view (/units/json/<id>?version=titans) shows the same string in the unit's game file.
  - PA Lobby does not say where the line comes from. This note names that italic line as a copy of the in-game description, so it is official text read through a faithful copy (the confidence list's high). Cite the unit page as kind database and say so in the source note, in your own words.
  - Some lines were rewritten with a rework: the Barnacle and Vanguard (April 2024), the Horsefly (June 2025) and the Icarus (July 2026). Read the live page.
- **How a line reads.** A type label, a dash, then a few short sentences, which often end with what the unit attacks.
  - The label is the designation for roles step 1.
  - The sentences after the dash are the official description. While a unit has a label, they never decide step 1; they count at roles.secondary step 1, as strong or weak wording, and as a target line (can_target step 3).
  - A playable commander's line is only its name (Imperial Able Commander), so the commander has no designation and step 1 gives nothing. The commanders table also holds four class base entries (Imperial, Quadruped, Raptor and Tank Class Commander) whose line is a placeholder; the one commander entry covers them all.
- **Designations that name a role** (a label or alias of the roles list, in any word form):
  - anti-air: Mobile Anti-Air (Spinner) and Anti-Air Bot (Stinger);
  - scout: Scout (Firefly, Skitter);
  - siege, through the alias bomber: Carpet Bomber (Bumblebee), Tactical Bomber (Hornet) and Siege Bomber (Wyrm). Siege's coding rule still binds: dropped bombs pass it; the Hornet's missiles pass only if a source says they are built mainly to destroy structures;
  - marksman, through the alias sniper: Sniper (Gil-E), as long as its weapon is of the sniper family and reaches long;
  - support: Support Barge (Barnacle, whose line limits its repairs to ships) and Support Platform (Angel); both repair other units;
  - transport: Air Transport (Pelican). It has one seat, so transport's coding rule fails and step 1 skips the role. The Astraeus (Orbital Lander) also has one seat, and its label names no role.
- **Designations that name no role**, so step 1 goes on:
  - land: Basic Infantry (Dox), Assault Bot, Assault Tank, Light Tank, Heavy Tank, Flame Tank, Hover Tank, Attack Vehicle, Mortar tank, Flak Tank, Tesla Bot, Nanobot Swarm, Bomb bot, Mobile Tactical Missile, Proxy Commander (Colonel), Jamming Vehicle, Mobile Anti-Nuke and Mobile Nuke;
  - air: Fighter, Advanced Interplanetary Fighter, Gunship, Strafer Aircraft and Solar Drone;
  - naval: Gunboat, Frigate, Submarine, Advanced Submarine, Deep Water Destroyer, Hover Destroyer, Missile Ship, Battleship and Drone Carrier;
  - builders: Basic, Advanced, Combat, Advanced Combat and Orbital Fabricator. Fabricator is not an engineer alias, so builders go on to step 2;
  - orbital: Orbital Fighter, Space Probe, Basic Radar, Advanced Radar, Economy (Solar Array), Orbital Laser Platform, Railgun Platform and Orbital Battleship;
  - titans: Seismic Titan, Rolling Fortress, Lightning Titan and Invasion Titan;
  - Fire Support (Grenadier): the roles list counts fire support as firepower.
- **Step 2 for the combat fabricators.** The Stitch and Mend carry only tools, and their lines put repairing first, ahead of building. Step 2 picks between support and engineer by their main action.
- **Role words after the dash** (roles.secondary step 1): mobile artillery (Sheller), an alias of siege, which still needs siege's coding rule; repairs (Stitch, Mend, Barnacle, Angel), an alias of support.
- **No strong-against or weak-against lines.** No description says a unit is good or poor against a kind of target. Apart from labels and role words, the lines give three things:
  - Target lines: land and sea, only air, everything but orbital, or no attack at all. PA Lobby's Targets line under each weapon gives its exact layers (Game-wide mechanics, Target layers).
  - Labels on weapons: the Leviathan's guns, which its line labels anti-ship and anti-land; the Stinger's anti-air missiles; and the Stingray's anti-air and tactical missiles. They count at can_target step 3 and at roles.secondary, never at step 1.
  - Traits that name no kind of target: devastating damage (Locusts, Leveler, Atlas, Wyrm), open to flanking (Leveler), fragile and slow (Bumblebee), out of reach of cannons, which means under water (Barracuda), near invincible (Ares), shoots down missiles (Gil-E, Angel) and hidden from radar (Kraken). Use them in strengths and weaknesses only, never at step 4 or for the rule that drops a role.
- **Step 4: no bonus in the game data.** Ammo armour maps hold only 0, 0.33 or 1 (Game-wide mechanics, Armour types), so no weapon does more than full damage to any kind of unit. Step 4 rests on two things only: a main weapon that can hit nothing else, or patch-note wording that the unit is strong against a kind of target.
  - Main weapons whose Targets line is Air alone give anti-air: the Spinner, Stinger, Storm, Hummingbird, Phoenix and Icarus.
- **The patch notes are official text.** They are the posts labelled Community Announcements on the game's Steam news feed, https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamNews/GetNewsForApp/v2/?appid=386070&count=40&maxlength=0&format=json, written since 2024 by the volunteer teams that the posts credit. The same feed carries press items (labelled GamingOnLinux and PCGamesN): never cite those as official text. Cite the feed's address and name the post's title and date in the source.
  - Role words, for roles.secondary step 1 (each still needs its role's requires): the Dox as the game's main raiding unit (11 April 2022, and again in June 2025); the Kestrel, meant for raiding (April 2024); the Wyrm, reworked into a bomber against bases (bomber, so siege; 26 July 2026); the Bumblebee, which keeps its area denial against bunched bots (area denial; 26 July 2026); the Boom, back to an anti-vehicle job (anti-armour; 26 July 2026). The Grenadiers' long-range support (April 2022) means firepower and names no role. The Bluehawk's use as an anti-vehicle and anti-orbital counter is in the past: the June 2025 and March 2026 posts make it a skirmisher, which names no role.
  - Weak points that name a kind, for the rule that drops a role: the Slammer, made a little worse against durable targets such as tanks (armour; June 2025); the Narwhal, made more open to T1 and T2 air (June 2025); the Horsefly, not meant to beat fighters on its own (air; June 2025).
  - Matchups the posts name: the Bumblebee as the main answer to T1 bots (April 2024); the Gil-E, the Hummingbird and the Stryker's anti-air among the Hornet's counters (April 2024, June 2025); the Stryker's anti-air aimed at the Hornet, Angel, Wyrm and Icarus (June 2025); Levelers without support meant to fall to swarms of Dox and Booms (April 2024); the Grenadier, quicker against static defences and more of a threat to slow T2 vehicles and commanders (April 2024); the Spark, strengthened against the Dox and Stryker (July 2026); the Narwhal, more open to the Piranha and Drifter (July 2026). The Icarus makes a poor escort (July 2026): a weakness that names no kind of target.
  - How to read them: a role label or alias counts at roles.secondary step 1. Strong-against wording counts at step 4 only when it names a kind of target: air or aircraft mean air; tanks, vehicles or anti-vehicle mean armour; infantry means infantry. The word bots on its own names no kind, because PA's bots run from the Dox to the Atlas. Check every post against the version researched: later patches change units.
- **Not official:** the Planetary Annihilation Wiki on Fandom (its own words, unit numbers from build 71937, and design proposals from 2012); Wikipedia; PA Lobby's T0 to T3 labels, the site's own (they follow the game's Basic, Advanced and Titan types, but commanders and the Kessler show T0); and the user tags on the Steam store page (Robots, Mechs).

### Planetary Annihilation: TITANS (`pa`)

Written in the batch R4 preparation (11 November 2026), before any `pa` unit is coded, and checked by a second researcher. Sources: PA Lobby's TITANS unit pages, tables and blueprint views, the Steam news feed named under Official role lines, the Steam store page, and the Planetary Annihilation Wiki's game page on Fandom, which copies the official feature list. A blueprint inherits what it does not set (armour type, command list, wreck fraction) from its base spec: base_bot, base_vehicle, base_flyer, base_ship, base_orbital, base_structure or base_commander, each at /units/json/<spec>?version=titans on palobby.com.

The game has one roster for every player, so every unit is `pa.shared.<slug>`.

- **Basic orders** (no pattern; leave off). Every mobile unit has move and patrol, and every one but the Helios has assist (the base specs' command lists; the Helios's blueprint sets its own list). Armed units also have attack; the Skitter got one in April 2024 only so that it can attack-move. Land units have use, for teleporters (exceptions under Teleporters). Fire stances (such as hold fire) and area orders exist too. The Fandom wiki's Area Commands, Order queueing and Retreat Zones pages are design proposals from 2012: never cite them as evidence.
- **Builders** (not game-wide: record on each builder).
  - Fabricators, the commander and the Colonel build, repair, reclaim and assist (command lists; Builds boxes). Code the build menu by the abilities rule: build-structure for factories, economy and sensor buildings; deploy-turret for defence towers; lay-mines for mines; build-linked-exits for teleporters; build-cover for walls. Repair is repair-allies.
  - Reclaim breaks wrecks and terrain down into resources for the side. Link gather-resources, whose salvage-wrecks variant covers it with no drop-off; research/registry-notes/patterns.md files PA's reclaim under that pattern. No fit_note.
  - Assisting, the assist order on another builder's construction or on a factory, is part of build-structure, never an ability of its own.
  - Exceptions, from their lines and boxes: the Stitch builds only mines and teleporters and cannot help other construction; the Mend adds defences to those; the Barnacle builds only mines and teleporters and cannot help build units. The Barnacle, Stitch, Mend and Angel repair nearby units on their own (Auto Repair box), and the Barnacle, Mend and Angel also reclaim wrecks on their own (Auto Reclaim box). Since October 2026 the Stitch and Mend go on building nearby structures of kinds they can build while they move (posts of 3 and 8 October 2026).
- **Streaming economy** (no pattern; leave off). Metal and energy come in as income, a builder spends both every second while it builds, and when income falls short all building slows (the March 2026 post calls this stalling).
  - Units that make metal or energy themselves, the commander, the Icarus and the Solar Array (Economy box): record a passive, source innate, with no pattern and a fit_note, because generate-income needs the unit to stop and set up.
- **Costs paid from the side's stock** (no resource).
  - A weapon whose PA Lobby entry gives a cost per shot draws it from the side's pool: energy for the Spark, the Boom's self-destruct, the Bumblebee, Wyrm, Icarus, Zeus, SXX-1304 and Artemis and the commander's Uber Cannon; metal for the Ward's missile and the Typhoon's drone launcher.
  - A Base energy consumption line is upkeep from the same pool: the Stingray, Nyx, ARKYD, Advanced Radar Satellite and Helios. Mobile radar needs that energy to work (April 2024).
  - The Resources list says a price paid from the side's shared stock is not a resource, as games-r5.md says for Dawn of War's global resource. Code no resource; say in the weapon's summary (for an interceptor, in armour.notes), or in sensors.notes for radar, that it draws on the side's energy or metal.
- **The commander** (one entry, `pa.shared.commander`, for every skin).
  - Every player starts with one: gate Start of the match, and no cost band, since it is never bought. PA Lobby's commanders table lists 76 with one shared stat block, in four body classes (Imperial, Quadruped, Raptor and Tank), plus a tutorial commander that is not researched.
  - It builds basic structures, makes metal and energy, and has storage. Its gun, anti-air missile and torpedo launcher fire on the attack order.
  - The Uber Cannon fires only on its own order (the uber_cannon blueprint turns manual fire on and automatic fire off), takes 10,000 energy from the side for each shot and can also hit aircraft. By Weapons vs abilities that makes it an ability: link fire-power-shot.
  - In the default mode, a player who loses every commander loses the match. Eradication (June 2025) and the other modes are game rules: leave them off.
  - The Colonel (Proxy Commander) is an ordinary T2 builder, not a commander.
- **No veterancy, capture, garrisons or crates.** No command list read has a capture order, and no page or post read mentions ranks or experience. No earn-veterancy, and no ability has source veterancy.
- **Wrecks** (on_death wreck, basis in-game).
  - Since June 2025 every unit leaves a wreck holding half its metal cost, which builders reclaim. Naval and hover wrecks sink (April 2023), and aircraft wrecks fall to the ground (April 2023, with the modding note of July 2026). A wreck stays visible in the fog once seen (hotfix of 7 July 2026).
  - Cite the June 2025 post, or name it in an uncertain entry.
  - Exceptions: units whose blueprint sets the wreck's health fraction to 0, which is every orbital unit (through base_orbital) and the Locusts. The Helios is no exception since July 2026: it crashes and leaves a wreck. For the exceptions, code what their own pages show, or else the decision-3C default, and add an uncertain entry, because no page says outright that a fraction of 0 means no wreck.
- **Death blasts** (on_death death-blast).
  - Only units whose PA Lobby page has a Death Explosion box with damage: every commander, the Ares, Atlas, Zeus and Helios (its crash, since July 2026), the Manhattan (a nuke on death) and the Jig, a structure. Those that also leave a wreck get both outcomes.
  - Since June 2025 the commander's and the titans' blasts spare allies, and the Helios crash added in July 2026 does too.
  - Self-destruct attacks (the Boom, Manhattan and Kessler) are weapons or abilities, not on_death outcomes.
- **Armour types** (no armour map, no damage map, no armour model).
  - Each blueprint gives the unit one of eight armour types by kind of unit: AT_Bot, AT_Vehicle, AT_Hover, AT_Air, AT_Naval, AT_Orbital, AT_Structure and AT_Commander. They grade no toughness, so no armour map fits them.
  - Some ammo scales its damage by armour type, only by 0, a third or full: flak and air-defence ammo do nothing to land units, ships or structures; the nuke launcher's missile and the Manhattan's blast do a third to commanders and orbital units; the commander's and the Jig's death nukes do full damage to commanders and none to orbital units; the titans' blasts do nothing to aircraft or orbital units.
  - For the field rules: no step 4 bonus exists (Official role lines); damage step 4 never applies, since PA has no damage map or damage categories; and armour-class step 2 never applies, since PA has no light, medium or heavy category. Description words such as heavy armored (Inferno) or heavily armored (Vanguard) belong to the job line, as the Red Alert 1 manual's armour grades did (games-r1.md).
  - Armour class therefore comes from steps 3 to 5. Step 3: the Leveler, the cost anchor, is heavy. Step 4: the kind of unit; the Ant, labelled Light Tank, is a light tank (medium), and the Vanguard, a Heavy Tank, is a battle tank (heavy). Step 5: HP on PA Lobby against the Leveler and the Dox, which check B makes light.
  - No page gives facing values, so never code directional. The Leveler's line calls it open to flanking, and its turret turns slowly: put that in its weaknesses.
- **Damage targets.** Every ammo read takes health (Damage target HitPoints), except the Locusts' beam, whose damage target is Metal (its Ammo box). No page read says what that does to the target: say so in its summary, with an uncertain entry.
- **Friendly fire.** PA Lobby flags the few ammo whose splash hurts allies; among the pages read, the Manhattan's nuke, the Jig's death nuke and the Unit Cannon's pods. Give friendly-fire only to weapons with that flag.
- **Burn damage.** Almost every ammo on PA Lobby lists a burn damage and radius, even the Dox's bullets and the death blasts. No page read says it hurts units over time: never code fire, damage-over-time or zone from it.
- **Target layers** (can_target). Each weapon's Targets line on PA Lobby lists its layers from the game data; it is a target line for can_target step 3. Read it as follows:
  - LandHorizontal: infantry, ground vehicles, and structures where the weapon's family allows them.
  - WaterSurface or Underwater: naval. A weapon whose line has neither cannot reach ships, which is the naval coding rule's exception.
  - Seafloor, the sea bed where amphibious units walk under water: no kind of its own; name it in the summary.
  - Air: low air and high air, since PA has one air layer.
  - Orbital: none of our kinds. Say so in the summary and add a fit_note wanting an orbital target; a weapon that reaches only orbital units lists no kind.
  - Leave out a kind that the weapon's ammo sets to 0 in its armour map.
- **Orbital units and planets** (fit_notes for the gaps).
  - Orbital units fly in a layer above the planet. Weapons that target the orbital layer hit them; anti-air such as the Storm and the Galata turret can also damage the Astraeus (April 2022 bug fixes), which drops to the air layer to load (July 2026).
  - Most orbital units are always visible to every player (Visibility box); the Astraeus, Hermes and ARKYD are not.
  - Units of the Interplanetary type fly between planets on their own, at speeds kept apart from their move speed: the Phoenix, Astraeus, Avenger, Omega, Hermes, ARKYD, Advanced Radar Satellite, SXX-1304, Artemis, Solar Array, orbital fabrication bot and Helios. Speed bands use the move speed; put the trip in notes.
  - The word lists have no orbital class, mobility or target kind. Until Mustafa decides whether to add them, code an orbital unit as class aircraft, with the mobility that counts as high air: jet when its speed band is fast or very fast, otherwise airship. List the rules it breaks (speed, tier) in atypical, and add a fit_note at mobility/base that names the orbital layer as the gap.
  - Planet-smashing weapons and nukes are side-wide superweapons: leave them off. The planet-smashers are the Halley and the Catalyst in the advanced builders' menus, and the Ragnarok.
- **Transports** (one passenger passive on the carrier; Paired entries).
  - The Pelican carries one land unit, never the commander. The Astraeus carries one land unit, or an air or naval fabricator, to another planet, the commander included (their blueprints' transporter blocks).
  - One seat each: crew.passengers with 1 seat, and never the transport role.
  - Since July 2026 a Dox riding in a Pelican can fire from it, and no other rider can (transporter block; July 2026 post). Code the Pelican's seat as passenger-firing, linking passenger-sets-weapon, and say in crew.notes that only a Dox fires. The Astraeus's seat is passenger-cargo, linking carry-passengers.
  - The Pelican's targeting weapon does no damage: it only slows the Pelican while an enemy land or naval unit is in its reach. Give it no weapon entry; put the slowdown in mobility.notes.
- **Teleporters** (build-linked-exits on their builders; nothing on the units that use them).
  - Teleporters are structures, built by the commanders, fabricators, Stitch, Mend, Barnacle, Colonel and orbital fabrication bot (the teleporter's Built By box).
  - Land units step through with the use order, on one planet or between planets: that is the universal enter key. A unit that cannot use them says so: no titan has the order, the orbital fabrication bot lost it in April 2024, and the Kaiju gained it then.
  - The Helios's link with a teleporter is the Helios's own ability.
- **Unit Cannon and factories** (structures; leave off). The T2 Unit Cannon launches up to 16 land units at once to any point in the system; being launchable may go in a unit's notes, and a launched unit keeps its own factory gate. An advanced factory also builds the basic units of its kind, which keep their basic gate.
- **Sight, radar, sonar and jamming** (sensor traits, per unit; Recon box).
  - Sight bands use the Vision radius (registry sight_reference). A radar or sonar radius (sonar is radar under water) gives the radar trait. Underwater, orbital and mine vision go in sensors.notes.
  - The Nyx hides nearby allies from enemy radar: the jammer trait (the Radar Jamming Station is a structure).
  - The Kraken is the only unit hidden from radar (Stealth box). Our stealth trait also hides a unit from sight, so give it no trait and add a fit_note, as for RA2's NightHawk.
  - The Skitter, Stitch, Mend and Barnacle find mines (mine vision). Code detector, with a fit_note saying that it finds only mines.
  - No unit cloaks, burrows or disguises itself.
- **Slowing while firing** (no pattern). The Stinger slows sharply while it fires (July 2026), and the Pelican near enemies (Transports). Speed bands use the listed move speed; put the slowdown in mobility.notes.
- **Shields** (none). A shield system was added for testing in March 2026 and shown as a prototype in May 2026; no unit in the data read carries one. The ignore-shields flag on some ammo belongs to that system: code no shield model.
- **Shooting down missiles and pods** (per unit; Anti Entity Targets box). The Gil-E shoots down tactical missiles, the Angel anti-air missiles, the Ward the nuke launcher's missile, and the Bluehawk and Stingray the Unit Cannon's pods. Code each by rule 8 of Weapon entries and the interceptor model's coding rule; what neither covers, such as guarding allies or downing pods, goes in a fit_note.
- **Mobility** (per unit; Physics box).
  - Amphibious, walking on the sea floor (the mobility trait amphibious): the Dox, Slammer, commander, Atlas, Colonel and Manhattan.
  - Hover over land, water and lava: the Drifter, Locusts, Kaiju, Ward and Ares (the Ares's hover shows in the hover table and its blueprint, not in its Physics box).
  - Water hover, on water only: the Piranha, Fabrication Ship and Barnacle.
- **Nature and class.** A unit its sources call a bot (Bot in its Unit Types box, a label such as Assault Bot, or a bot factory as its maker) or a drone (Solar Drone) is a robot or drone: nature uncrewed-machine. The drone class's size rule then decides whether it is a drone or is classed by how it moves. No page read says whether the tanks, aircraft, ships, orbital units or commanders carry crews, so their nature follows the nature list's coding rule unless their own sources say they are robots.
- **Game modes** (leave off): Eradication, Bounty Mode, Dynamic Alliances with alliance victory, and the ranked 1v1 ladder. Galactic War's tech cards, sub-commanders and AI factions are not researched.
- **Expansion** (introduced_in). TITANS includes the original game. Units missing from PA Lobby's Classic version get introduced_in `pa-titans`: the Stryker, Spark, Stinger, Locusts, Drifter, Storm, Manhattan, Nyx, Ward, Icarus, Horsefly, Wyrm, Angel, Typhoon, Kaiju, Omega, Hermes, Artemis, Kessler, Colonel and Barnacle, and the four mobile titans. The Nyx, Ward and Kessler came with the June 2025 update: say so in their notes.

Tables: /units/table/<name>?version=titans (mobile, builders, orbital, radar, titans, factories and more). Blueprints: /units/json/<id>?version=titans; the weapon and ammo files are linked from the unit page, and the base specs (base_bot and the others named under Game-wide mechanics) hold what a unit inherits. /units/json/base_unit is not served.

A line that is missing means zero: the Recon box leaves out a vision of 0 that the tables show.
  - Already in the page cache: every buildable mobile unit's page, every ammo blueprint and the Steam news feed. The weapon blueprints and the ammo files of the two dummy weapons are not.
- **Patch notes.** Read the Steam news feed (Official role lines) with the page reader, which prints it post by post. Steam's own post pages and the Steam Community announcement pages give no post text. Cite the feed's address and name the post's title and date in the source; in other text, name a post by its date, because some titles run to six words or more and the copy-check flags them.
- **The Planetary Annihilation Fandom wiki** is an old, thin stub (its unit list is from build 71937). Do not use it for numbers. Its Commander page mixes Legion structures into the build list, keeps the old death-blast numbers and says the blast hurts allies, which stopped in June 2025.
- **Cost anchor.** The balance post of 11 April 2022 calls the Ant (T1, Light Tank, 150 metal) the game's intended main battle tank, while the registry anchors on the Leveler (its basis says why). Until Mustafa decides, keep the Leveler anchor; the Ant stays a light tank for its armour class (Game-wide mechanics, Armour types).
- **Range against sight.** Many long weapons reach past their own unit's Vision radius, and off-screen's first reason then applies: the Leveler's gun (120 against the Dox's 75) is long by its reach and passes its own sight (100), so it bands off-screen. Check every long weapon against its unit's own vision.
- **Traps.**
  - The Skitter has no real weapon: the dummy tool it got in April 2024 only stops it rushing in when attack-moved.
  - The Pelican's weapon only aims (Game-wide mechanics, Transports). The Typhoon's weapon does no damage: it launches Squall drones, which are not buildable units.
  - The Ward's missile (0.01 damage) is an anti-nuke interceptor, and the Angel's beam and the Gil-E's second beam shoot down missiles (Game-wide mechanics, Shooting down missiles and pods).
  - The Barracuda's line says cannons cannot target it: it is under water. Its radar stealth was removed in April 2022.
  - The commander is one entry for 76 skins (Game-wide mechanics).
- **Sites to cite**, one page of each for the plant test (handoff, section 3):
  - palobby.com, a unit page: https://palobby.com/units/unit/assault_bot?version=titans (the site passed on 11 November 2026);
  - palobby.com, a blueprint view: https://palobby.com/units/json/assault_bot?version=titans (3 of 3 flagged in the prep's check; test it in the site test, since coders cite it for blueprint fields such as the wreck fraction, the transporter block and manual fire);

  - store.steampowered.com: https://store.steampowered.com/app/386070/Planetary_Annihilation_TITANS/ (4 of 5 flagged; the miss is a news teaser that the page draws by script);
  - planetaryannihilation.fandom.com: https://planetaryannihilation.fandom.com/wiki/Planetary_Annihilation (the site passed on 11 November 2026);
  - optional and untested: en.wikipedia.org, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetary_Annihilation;
  - not cited: planetaryannihilation.com, which answers HTTP 403 and whose archived copies would not load. Liquipedia is not used for this game.
- **Corrections to step 1's notes above** (the lines they replace are removed):
  - Tiers, in place of the two bullets on the titans' gate and the orbital fabrication bot: titans use the gate `Titan (built by an advanced fabricator or the orbital fabrication bot)`, band t3. The T1 orbital fabrication bot, made at the T1 Orbital Launcher, builds all four mobile titans and is the Helios's only builder, and its own line says it builds titans (Built By and Builds boxes). So t3 rests on the game's own Titan type (Unit Types box; PA Lobby's T3), not on the length of the tech path: say so in tier.basis and in the source note.
  - Speed, in place of the bullet on every tank at speed 10: most tanks (speed 10) and most bots (12 to 14) are very slow or slow; the Drifter hover tank and the Stryker attack vehicle move at 14, which is slow. The Boom moves at 40 (2.0, fast), and the Locusts at 30 since March 2026 (1.5, medium, at the boundary like the Zeus); the Boom, Skitter and Locusts all outpace the Dox on land. The Dox's 20 is the speed it really moves at: the April 2022 update raised it from 19 and cut its acceleration, yet it still reaches full speed in under half a second, and nothing slows it while it fires.
  - Prices, in place of Uncertain item 4: PA cost bands follow tech level only loosely. T1 runs from very low through low (the ships Narwhal, Barracuda, Barnacle and Orca) and medium (the ARKYD) to high (the orbital fabrication bot); T2 runs from low (the Locusts, Slammer and Nyx at 500) to very high, with the Mend medium and the advanced fabricators and the Colonel very high.

### MechWarrior / BattleTech (`mechwarrior`)

Written in the batch R4 preparation (11 November 2026), before any `mechwarrior` unit is coded, and checked by a second researcher, from the BattleTechWiki's unit role pages and its two role categories, its Master Unit List, InfoBoxBattleMech and 'Mech pages, the MechWarrior Online Wiki's 'Mech pages, and the official MechWarrior Online and MechWarrior 5: Clans sites. It replaces the Official role lines bullet that step 1 left under Research notes for the r4 agents.

- **Designation: the unit role.** The rulebooks the role pages cite (the Introductory Rulebook of Classic BattleTech, the two Alpha Strike books and Campaign Operations) define a set of battlefield roles, and the Master Unit List (MUL), Catalyst Game Labs' official unit database, gives units their role (the role pages link MUL searches by role). Read the role of the MUL entry for the model researched as its designation for roles step 1, and cite the MUL as kind official.
- **Which roles name ours.** The Unit Roles category (https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Category:Unit_Roles) lists fourteen: Ambusher, Attack Fighter, Brawler, Dogfighter, Fast Dogfighter, Fire Support, Interceptor, Juggernaut, Missile Boat, Scout, Skirmisher, Sniper, Striker and Transport.
  - Six of them are roles for aircraft and aerospace craft, never for a 'Mech: Attack Fighter, Dogfighter, Fast Dogfighter, Fire Support, Interceptor and Transport (https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Fire_Support, https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Transport). The ground roles are the eight in https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Category:BattleMech_Roles: Ambusher, Brawler, Juggernaut, Missile Boat, Scout, Skirmisher, Sniper and Striker.
  - Scout is our scout label and Sniper is an alias of marksman, so a 'Mech's role can name one of ours only as Scout or Sniper; the other six ground roles are none of our labels or aliases. Transport would be our transport label, and Fire Support names no role (support meaning firepower), but both are aircraft roles.
  - Marksman still has its coding rule: a Sniper whose long-range guns are not in our sniper family fails it, and step 1 goes on.
- **The MUL cannot be read today.** The BattleTechWiki's Master Unit List page (https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Master_Unit_List) says MUL 2.0 replaced the old site on 31 August 2026. The masterunitlist.info unit links on the wiki's pages now fail (the Centurion's answered HTTP 404), and the new site, https://masterunitlist.battletech.com/, refused the page reader (HTTP 403, 11 November 2026). The BattleTechWiki's 'Mech pages do not give the role: InfoBoxBattleMech has no role field (its seldom-used Use field is the wiki's words, and its usage instructions leave it out), the role pages describe each role without listing units (their MUL links still point at the old site), and a text search of the wiki found no 'Mech page that names its MUL role.
- **Trap: BattleMech Combat Categories.** https://www.sarna.net/wiki/BattleMech_Combat_Categories sits in the BattleMech Roles category beside the role pages and names example 'Mechs for seven categories (the Atlas as a juggernaut, the Jenner as a striker, the Spider as a scout, the Panther as a sniper). It is an edited retelling of four pages of the old Introductory Rulebook, and its own header warns that this source is out of date. It is not the MUL and not a designation: never read a role from it, at roles step 1 or at roles.secondary step 1.
- **So every 'Mech starts at roles step 2.** While the MUL cannot be read, leave it out of sources and add an uncertain entry at roles/primary that says it could not be read. Then go on: step 2 (not a fighter), step 3 (siege for a lobbed main weapon that reaches long or further, such as artillery, or a long-range missile the sources say is built mainly against structures; marksman only for our sniper family), step 4 (see Strong-against below), step 5.
- **Technical Readouts.** A readout's own text on a design (its Capabilities section and the rest) is official, but the BattleTechWiki does not copy it: its Description and Weapons and Equipment sections retell it in the wiki's words, with page references, so they are not official text. The infobox's weight class (Ultralight, Light, Medium, Heavy, Assault, Superheavy) is filled in from the mass; it is the armour map's key, not a role. Every edition of MechWarrior 5: Clans comes with a digital game manual, and its Deluxe edition (Digital Extras on the official site) with a readout of its own; both are official, and neither is on the web.
- **The piloted games give no role line.** No official 'Mech role or description line was found for MechWarrior Online or MechWarrior 5: Clans.
  - mwomercs.com has official pages for the 'Mechs it sells as packs or Legends (such as https://mwomercs.com/packages/perseus and https://mwomercs.com/legends/Onyx). They list specs, hardpoints by location and top speed, with no role or description line. The store index draws its list by script, so take a pack's address from the news post that announces it. The site's Game menu has only Overview, Patch Notes and Download, and its game-manual link leads back to the overview.
  - mw5clans.com has no 'Mech pages; its DLC pages give only the names of the new 'Mechs.
  - The MechWarrior Online Wiki's 'Mech descriptions are its own words. MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries has an in-game 'Mech database with descriptions, but Mercenaries is not a counted title, so that text never counts.
- **Patch notes and news posts.** The piloted games' patch notes are official text: mwomercs.com/game/patch-notes and the Steam news feed for app 342200, and the release notes in the news on mw5clans.com; so are the two sites' news posts. The newest notes are https://mwomercs.com/game/patch-notes/3116 (20 October 2026) and, for Clans, https://mw5clans.com/news/2026/02/180-mw5-clans-patch-notes-and-update (6 February 2026). A role label or alias there that describes a 'Mech's own job counts at roles.secondary step 1, and a weak point there feeds its drop rule; it is never a designation for step 1. Read role words by the roles word list's rules: the February 2026 notes call the Arrow IV a support weapon, and support meaning firepower names none. A pack announcement such as the Perseus Booster Pack post (19 October 2026) uses sales words and names no role.
- **Strong-against and weak-against.** No source has official lines, so step 4 rests on the game data or on a main weapon that can hit nothing else.
  - The game data gives two weapons extra damage against infantry: the Damage field of the Machine Gun's infobox gives it 2 damage, and 2D6 against infantry, and the Flamer's gives 2, and 4D6 against infantry, both from Total Warfare's table for burst-fire weapons against infantry (https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Machine_Gun, https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Flamer). Of the counted titles, only the tabletop's pages read speak to damage against infantry, so the tabletop decides (Series games). A 'Mech whose main weapon is machine guns or flamers is anti-infantry at step 4 (the Firestarter FS9-H lists its four flamers first), and such a secondary weapon supports anti-infantry at roles.secondary step 3. Read any other weapon's Damage field the same way. The figure after OR in those fields (8B/6B on the Machine Gun) comes from A Time of War, the role-playing game, which is not a counted title.
  - The bracket tags in a weapon's Type field (anti-infantry on the Machine Gun, Flamer and Plasma rifle) and the wiki's prose calling those weapons deadly to infantry are the wiki's words: they count only for the roles.secondary label clause (see Words in brackets, under Damage in the research notes), never for step 4.
  - A target list that is short only because MechWarrior Online has almost nothing but 'Mechs to shoot at does not count as hitting nothing else (roles.secondary).
- **Sides.** A design is one entry whichever side fields it, so the rule that official text must hold for every side's version only matters for an archetype recorded once for several designs.
mechwarrior.game_wide:
### MechWarrior / BattleTech (`mechwarrior`)

Written in the research run's batch preparation, before any mechwarrior unit is coded, from the BattleTechWiki's BattleMech, Physical Attacks, Jump Jet, Heat Sink, OmniMech, Mechanized Battle Armor, List of Design Quirks and MechWarrior 5: Clans pages, and the MechWarrior Online Wiki's Beginners Guide: Interface/Basics, Heat Sinks, Heat Scaling, Critical Hit, Armor, Module and Quirks pages. The MechWarrior Online Wiki pages are old (those read were last edited between 2014 and 2021), so check MechWarrior Online facts against its patch notes. The counted titles are the tabletop designs, MechWarrior Online and MechWarrior 5: Clans (see Series games). Checked again in the R4 prep on 11 November 2026 against those pages, the BattleTechWiki's MechWarrior 5: Clans/BattleMechs and Sensors pages, MechWarrior Online's overview page (https://mwomercs.com/game) and patch notes, and MechWarrior 5: Clans' Elementals preview, DLC pages and patch notes (see the research notes for their addresses).

- **Basic controls** (throttle, turning the legs, torso twist and centring the torso, full stop, powering down and up, targeting an enemy to see its weapons and damage and to lock guided missiles, weapon groups, chain fire and alpha strike, zoom, night and heat vision): every 'Mech. No pattern. Torso twist is how a biped 'Mech aims, not an ability; quads cannot twist without a design quirk. The mount proposal follows the aim-models tie-break, which counts a torso that twists only partway as limited arc. The MechWarrior Online Wiki's variant infoboxes give how far the torso twists (torso yaw 100 on https://mwo.fandom.com/wiki/Centurion_CN9-A), a sourced basis for that arc.
- **Orders to teammates** (no pattern): MechWarrior 5: Clans gives the player a Command Wheel and a Battle Grid to direct the rest of the star, and in MechWarrior Online one player per team can place battle-plan markers. These are basic orders: leave them off.
- **Heat** (resource heat; no pattern): every 'Mech gains heat from firing, moving and jumping, and sheds it through heat sinks; past its limit it shuts down. In MechWarrior Online the pilot can override the shutdown for a few seconds, at the risk of internal damage and an ammunition explosion; MechWarrior 5: Clans has an override too (its February 2026 patch notes mention the voice line that announces it). Code heat as the resource on every 'Mech; shutdown and override belong to it and are not abilities. MechWarrior Online's heat scaling ("ghost heat") adds extra heat when too many of certain weapons fire at once: mention it in the summary of a weapon it affects (the patch of 20 October 2026 still tunes it, raising the LRMs' penalty). Equipment that dumps heat on a key (a coolant pod and the like) belongs to the design that carries it.
- **Ammunition** (resource limited-ammo, where that field's rule fits): ballistic and missile weapons feed from ammunition carried in the 'Mech. The only refill during a fight in the pages I read is MechWarrior 5: Clans' ammo caches, tagged in scan mode.
- **Locations and critical hits** (armour model zonal): every 'Mech's armour and structure are split by location (head, torso sections with front and rear armour, arms, legs). Once a location's armour is gone, hits can wreck the weapons and equipment inside it, ammunition included, before the location itself is destroyed. Code zonal on every 'Mech; it is built into the armour, and the model's examples name this game. Ammunition-protection equipment (CASE) belongs to the design: mention it in armour.notes.
- **Rear armour** (armour model directional, by the design's own values): code directional only when a cited page gives the design's rear torso armour as thinner than its front (a record sheet, or a page with armour by location), and say in armour.notes, in words, how much thinner. No page read does: the BattleTechWiki's infobox names only the kind of armour, the MechWarrior Online pages give a total, and in MechWarrior Online each torso location shares its armour allowance with its rear, so the split is a loadout choice (MechWarrior Online Wiki, Armor). No rule read makes rear hits do more by themselves. Otherwise leave directional off, and say in armour.notes that each torso section has rear armour of its own, whose value no cited page gives.
- **Physical attacks** (tabletop; no pattern): as its build allows, a 'Mech can punch with its arms, push, kick, charge, or swing something it has picked up, and one with jump jets can make a death-from-above attack. These come with being a 'Mech: leave them off weapons and abilities. A melee weapon the design carries (a hatchet and the like) is a weapon of our melee family. No page read shows 'Mech melee in MechWarrior Online or MechWarrior 5: Clans (the MechWarrior Online Wiki's FAQ, written before launch, says in one place that melee was not being considered and in another that it was planned). The melee variants on some BattleTechWiki pages (the Centurion's CN9-P with a mace) come from MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries, which is not counted.
- **Jump jets** (mobility trait leap; pattern leap): not game-wide. Only designs that mount them can jump; record them on those units. Jumping heats the 'Mech and makes it harder to hit, but spoils its own aim (Jump Jet page). Since the free update that came with Wolves of Tukayyid, MechWarrior 5: Clans' jets push the 'Mech the way the pilot steers (BattleTechWiki's MechWarrior 5: Clans page; https://mw5clans.com/dlc/wolves-of-tukayyid, under free updates): say so in the leap ability's summary.
- **Speed and electronic equipment**: not game-wide. MASC, triple-strength myomer and superchargers, and electronics such as ECM, active probes, TAG and Narc, belong to the designs that carry them; record them on those units (patterns.md gives MASC as an overclock-self example, and an always-on ECM is the jammer trait). The standard sensors and the electronic-warfare features every 'Mech has, which make it harder to lock onto (the BattleMech page), give no sensor trait. Neither does the basic sensor data that every combat unit's targeting and tracking system can pass to friendly units (BattleTechWiki's Sensors page).
- **Variants, OmniMech configurations and refits** (no pattern): a design's variants, an OmniMech's pod configurations and MechLab refits are chosen before a battle, never during one, so they are not abilities or modes. Code the model researched; other configurations follow the armament rules for loadout picks, or go in notes. MechWarrior 5: Clans' MechLab also lets Clan BattleMechs fit or drop jump jets and MASC and swap engines between missions: record jets and MASC only when the stock model has them.
- **Design quirks** (no pattern): the tabletop's optional quirks and MechWarrior Online's per-variant quirks mostly change numbers: put those in notes. Record a quirk as a passive only when it adds a mechanic. A quirk that changes rolls or numbers, for the 'Mech or for units near it (Command 'Mech, Distracting), is a number change: notes only. The Rumble Seat quirk (a second seat for a passenger) was dropped from the BattleMech Manual: it gives no passenger seat.
- **Progression** (no pattern): MechWarrior Online's skill tree and MechWarrior 5: Clans' 'Mech XP upgrades and pilot skills improve a 'Mech outside the fight. Bands use the stock 'Mech; notes can name them.
- **Consumables and call-in strikes** (side-wide powers): in MechWarrior Online the player fits consumables (artillery and air strikes, Cool Shot coolant and others) into a 'Mech's consumable slots. They are the player's kit, not the design's: leave them off. MechWarrior 5: Clans' Wolves of Tukayyid DLC lets the player call artillery strikes onto a point picked on the Battle Grid (since the February 2026 patch they land where they are aimed): a side-wide power, left off too.
- **Elemental Point** (MechWarrior 5: Clans, Ghost Bear: Flash Storm DLC; side-wide support, no pattern on any 'Mech): in that DLC's missions a Point of Elementals fights beside the player's Star. It attacks nearby enemies by itself, can be sent at a chosen target through the command wheel, finishes off an enemy 'Mech whose head armour is gone, and comes back a while after it is wiped out; enemy Points jump onto a 'Mech and cling to it, doing some damage (https://mw5clans.com/news/2025/04/144-elementals). It belongs to no 'Mech design: leave it off every 'Mech. If an Elemental is coded as a unit, record these on that unit (see the research notes).
- **Scan mode** (MechWarrior 5: Clans; no pattern): every pilot can switch to a mode, with weapons unable to fire, for hacking turret controls, disarming mines, opening locks and tagging salvage and ammo caches. Leave it off.
- **Repair and salvage** (no pattern): technicians repair 'Mechs between missions in MechWarrior 5: Clans, and the pages describe no repair during a fight. Leave it off.
- **Riding battle armour** (tabletop; carry-passengers would be the pattern): most OmniMechs have handholds that let friendly battle armour ride them into battle (six suits at most, twice that on superheavy 'Mechs), and other 'Mechs can carry riders only when the riders have magnetic clamps. The riders hang on outside rather than sit in seats, so give the 'Mech no passenger seats and leave the riding off it; say in crew.notes that an OmniMech can carry riders. Riders add a little protection to the OmniMech that carries them (OmniMech page), and clamps slow a standard 'Mech that carries riders (Mechanized Battle Armor page): crew.notes can say both. MechWarrior 5: Clans' Elementals do not ride friendly 'Mechs in the pages read. If battle armour is coded, record riding on it as its own (see Uncertain, in the research notes).
- **Capturing bases** (a game-mode rule, no pattern): the capture points of MechWarrior Online's Assault and Conquest modes. Other game-mode rules stay off as well: MechWarrior Online's Event Queue modifiers (Unlimited Ammo, Extra Armor) and Faction Play's four 'Mechs per match, and MechWarrior 5: Clans' Arena and Horde modes (Trials of War).
mechwarrior.research_notes:
### MechWarrior / BattleTech (`mechwarrior`)

Rewritten in the batch R4 preparation (11 November 2026), before any `mechwarrior` unit is coded. It replaces step 1's MechWarrior bullet under Research notes for the r4 agents (its role lines are now under Official role lines), the game's heading under Tiers that were hard to map, its two pointers under Damage and armour maps and Flavour affinity, and its item under Uncertain. What was right there is kept word for word.

- **Sites and page names.**
  - Sarna (BattleTechWiki), API at `https://www.sarna.net/wiki/api.php`. Mech pages need the `(BattleMech)` suffix when the name is ambiguous ("Centurion" alone is a disambiguation). Clan designs carry their Inner Sphere name in brackets: `Timber Wolf (Mad Cat)`, `Nova (Black Hawk)`, `Dire Wolf (Daishi)`, `Executioner (Gladiator)`, `Fire Moth (Dasher)`, and the battle armour `Elemental (Battle Armor)`.
  - The MechWarrior Online Wiki (mwo.fandom.com), read through https://mwo.fandom.com/api.php, since a plain page request gets HTTP 403. Its pages are old (those read were last edited between 2014 and 2021): use it only for game-specific mechanics, such as hardpoints and ghost heat, and check them against the patch notes. Its variant pages (such as https://mwo.fandom.com/wiki/Centurion_CN9-A) give the stock engine, speed, hardpoints and how far the torso twists. Never take a quirk from it: MechWarrior Online changes quirks often (patch 3116 alone changed several), and quirks are numbers for notes anyway.
  - mwomercs.com, MechWarrior Online's official site. Patch notes: the list at https://mwomercs.com/game/patch-notes, each patch at /game/patch-notes/<number>; the newest is 3116 (20 October 2026). Take the newest patch at coding time and name it in sources[].version. Pack and Legends pages (/packages/<name>, /legends/<name>) are official sources for MechWarrior Online play facts, such as the hardpoint type that damage step 4 can read. Only 'Mechs sold that way have one; none was found for the CN9-A.
  - mw5clans.com, MechWarrior 5: Clans' official site: release notes in its news, the newest for Clans at https://mw5clans.com/news/2026/02/180-mw5-clans-patch-notes-and-update (6 February 2026, live from 10 February). Its news feed also carries MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries (Chaos Reign in May 2026 and Ashes & Ascension in October 2026 are Mercenaries DLCs) and sales: check that a post is about Clans before citing it. DLC pages: https://mw5clans.com/dlc/ghost-bear-flash-storm and https://mw5clans.com/dlc/wolves-of-tukayyid.
  - Steam news, not needed so far (MechWarrior Online Legends is app 342200, MechWarrior 5: Clans app 2000890). Since commit 42364f7 the page reader and the copy-check read the feed post by post: cite https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamNews/GetNewsForApp/v2/?appid=342200&count=40&maxlength=0&format=json with the post's title and date, after a plant test of the feed.
  - Not citable: masterunitlist.battletech.com refuses the page reader (HTTP 403; see Official role lines).
- **Site test.** One page per site, plant-tested in this prep on 11 November 2026, every planted passage flagged (5 of 5): https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Centurion_(BattleMech) (browser), https://mwo.fandom.com/wiki/Centurion_CN9-A (the wiki's rendered page from its API, as the browser got HTTP 403), https://mwomercs.com/game/patch-notes/3116 (browser) and https://mw5clans.com/news/2026/02/180-mw5-clans-patch-notes-and-update (browser). A mwomercs.com pack or Legends page is a different kind of page. In this prep the copy-check flagged every passage planted from the cached https://mwomercs.com/legends/Onyx (three) and https://mwomercs.com/packages/perseus (one), but without a browser's view of the page: run the plant test on one before a unit cites it.
- **Versions.** MechWarrior 5: Clans counts with its DLCs and free updates (version_researched): Ghost Bear: Flash Storm (May 2025: Clan BattleMechs such as the Kodiak, the Elemental Point, engine swaps) and Wolves of Tukayyid (December 2025: more 'Mechs, the Arrow IV and artillery call-ins) are paid; Trials of War (now built into the game), the vectored jump jets and the MechLab updates are free. The BattleTechWiki tags its MechWarrior 5: Clans pages as apocryphal (outside the setting's canon); that does not stop them being sources for how the game plays.
- **Which 'Mechs MechWarrior 5: Clans covers.** The player pilots only Clan 'Mechs: OmniMechs, and from Ghost Bear: Flash Storm some Clan BattleMechs. Inner Sphere 'Mechs appear only as enemies, with models taken from MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries (https://www.sarna.net/wiki/MechWarrior_5:_Clans/BattleMechs, Non-playable table). That table names models and nothing of how they play, so it does not cover the 'Mech in the sense of Which title decides: MechWarrior Online decides how an Inner Sphere design plays.

The brief names this game for its mech archetypes (docs/brief.md).
  - **Weight class as a cost proxy, if a cost band is ever needed:** light → low, medium → medium, heavy → high, assault → very high. I did not put this in the entry.
- **The `armour_map` is a weight-class proxy.**
  - BattleTech has no named armour categories: armour is points per location.
  - Mapping: light and medium 'Mechs → medium ("light walkers"), heavy and assault → heavy (the class text names assault mechs), superheavy → super-heavy.
